subject: clients/web: use dedicated library to connect to SSE
message:
clients/web: use dedicated library to connect to SSE

The builtin EventSource class doesn't support to pass custom headers to the request, like Authorization.

From what I read, this class is somewhat deprecated and browser developers encourage to use `fetch` instead. The thing is, it's a much lower level API which doesn't do the work of reading and parsing the stream. Ref: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2177

I found `event-source-plus`, a library which does all that work on top of `fetch`.

subject: server/event: add ingested_at to events and use it when computing billing and balance
message:
server/event: add ingested_at to events and use it when computing billing and balance

This is important because we rely on the "last considered event" to know where
to start billing/balance computation on each run.

Since we allow to set arbitrary timestamp when ingesting events, we would take the risk
of ignoring events that may have been ingested after the last considered event, but with an
older timestamp.

To avoid this, we add an ingested_at timestamp to the events,
and use it to know the starting point.

subject: server/subscription: fix product upgrade when meters are the same
message:
server/subscription: fix product upgrade when meters are the same

The SQLAlchemy append event is fired for each item, even when we assign directly a full list. The effect of this when updating is that we basically start from scratch, leading to removing existing Subscription Meters. Then, when we re-add the same meter, we actually create a duplicate row.

To prevent this, we use the `bulk_replace` event instead, which gives us the whole list at once.

Fix #5922

subject: Backoffice[DatatableActions]: Use HTML-popover based Dropdown
message:
Backoffice[DatatableActions]: Use HTML-popover based Dropdown

We switch to using the new HTML-based popover attribute for the dropdown
in DatatableActions, as the old CSS-based one would be cut off by the
table bounding box meaning that it would not be visible when used in the
last row.

This was due to the table having `position: relative` and a parent
component having `overflow-x-auto`. We can't remove those because they
allow for nice scroll behavior on small screens.

See: https://daisyui.com/components/dropdown/#method-2-popover-api-and-anchor-positioning

message:
server: pin Python patch version in Docker build

* Pin the Python version to `3.12.11` in `pyproject.toml`. This will ensure UV automatically install the right version, no matter the version on the host machine. This is the source of truth for the Python version we want to execute.
* Fix the GitHub workflow so it installes the Python version set in `pyproject.toml` instead of `.python-version`.
* Loosen the constraint in `.python-version` and `Dockerfile` to just "3". It means that we don't really care about the system version: we only want it to execute UV, which will handle the Python version for us.

This should ensure that the Python version used in development and production is always the same.

subject: server: add tzdata-legacy package to Docker build
message:
server: add tzdata-legacy package to Docker build

In #6421, we discovered a bug where some valid timezones where rejected in production, while they were working in development.

To get a list of valid timezones, Python relies by default on the zoneinfo present on the Unix system.

It turns out that some timezones names are considered "legacy", like "Asia/Calcutta", which official name is now "Asia/Kolkata". It looks like those legacy names are no longer included in recent/slim Debian builds.

The solution is to explicitly add the `tzdata-legacy` package to the Docker build, which contains those legacy timezones.

Ref:
* https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html
* https://askubuntu.com/questions/1532129/difference-in-time-zone-data

subject: server/auth: fallback to Anonymous subject instead of erroring if not allowed subject
message:
server/auth: fallback to Anonymous subject instead of erroring if not allowed subject

Since we're checking authentication in the middleware, we try every possible authentication schemes available.

Thus, we can be in a situation where a user is both connected as a User to Polar, but also try to access the customer portal as a Customer.

Since we always prioritise Customer over User, it works most of the time. However, when connecting the GitHub or Discord benefit, the callback doesn't have the customer session token in the request. To solve that, we rely on the state to resolve the authenticated customer. However, it the user is authenticated as a User, we would have an error since we're trying to access that callback endpoint that only accepts Customer/Anonymous subjects.

This fix removes the error in case of wrong subject and falls back to the Anonymous subject instead; so we have more graceful handling of this kind of situation.

server/subscription: reset meters when creating the subscription

Before, we were only doing it when we received a new order (creation or cycle).

The problem is that, right after creation, we also enqueue the benefits, which might also include a meter credit benefit. It's possible then to have a race condition where the benefit is processed before the order, leading to credits that are immediately reset.

This change makes sure we also reset the meters right after creating the subscription, before enqueuing the benefits. Besides, we only reset them on cycle orders, so we don't reset them twice.

server/benefit/grant: reset revoked_at when granting a benefit again, even if there is an action required error

A benefit can be revoked and granted again, for example after a past due invoice that gets paid.

When granting again, we can hit an action required error. In that case, we should reset the revoked_at field to None, so that the benefit is considered active again, and the customer can see it in their dashboard.

Otherwise, the benefit would remain in a revoked state, and the customer would not see it in their dashboard, even though they have an active benefit that just requires action.

subject: server/webhook: introduce mechanism to ensure webhook events are delivered in order
message:
server/webhook: introduce mechanism to ensure webhook events are delivered in order

Webhook events can sometimes be delivered out of order. This change
introduces a mechanism to ensure events are processed in the order
they were generated.

The implementation works by having the worker check for earlier undelivered events
for the same webhook before delivering the current event. If any earlier events
are found, the current event is re-queued for later processing.

This approach isn't completely foolproof since earlier events might still be
in uncommitted database transactions, but it provides sufficient ordering
guarantees for most use cases.

subject: server: fix session.stream() usage
message:
server: fix session.stream() usage

It turns out that by default, calling `session.stream()` still buffers
the entire result set in memory, which is not what we want for large
datasets.

To achieve that behavior we actually need to set the `yield_per` argument in
`execution_options`.

The caveat with that is that we need to be careful to not try to stream when we
have result sets with one-to-many relationships, because then the ORM can't
apply its `unique()` magic on them.

In this commit, I've reviewed all usages of `session.stream()` and added
`yield_per` where appropriate, and made sure we don't use it in cases where
we have one-to-many relationships.

Apparently, there is an old root certificate that has been removed from recent CA bundles, but apparently still around in the wild.

What we do here is to pin certifi to a version that still includes this old root certificate.

However, we also include a CI check to ensure that we will be notified when this pinning can be removed.

subject: dx: reorganize Zed settings and enable running Pytest from Zed
message:
dx: reorganize Zed settings and enable running Pytest from Zed

Zed is able to handle Pytest tests out-of-the-box, but it always runs them from the root directory; which doesn't work for us since we have `.env` config and such in the `server/` directory.

It turns out this feature relies on the Tasks feature of Zed. When it detects a pytest test, it enables the "Run Test" action, with the tags "python-pytest-class"/"python-pytest-method".

Thus, we can define a task and overload the default command using those tags, where we make sure to run tests from the `server/` directory.

Ref:

* https://zed.dev/docs/tasks#binding-runnable-tags-to-task-templates
* https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/12aba6193e07f7f353983d051cc96c59688db6ab/crates/languages/src/python.rs#L795-L809

- Updated ProductPricingSection form validation to allow $0 for seat prices

subject: server/product: fix eager load error triggered after attached custom fields validation error
message:
server/product: fix eager load error triggered after attached custom fields validation error

When we validate custom fields, we remove all the existing fields, and create a savepoint. If one of the new fields is invalid, we rollback to the savepoint, which removes all the newly created fields. This behavior apparently invalidates all the eagerly loaded relationships, like prices, causing an error when we try to access them later in the request lifecycle.

The fix is to first make the prices validation, and do the custom fields validation at the end.

subject: feat(events): Add transitive closure
message:
feat(events): Add transitive closure

The closure allows us to easily query a sub-hierarchy of events (either from the root, or from any point in the tree),
to be able to count events, or aggregate different attributes on the events. By using and keeping a closure
we can do queries such as

```
SELECT * FROM events
LEFT JOIN events_closure ON events_closure.ancestor_id=events.id
```

Instead of having to do a recursive CTE.

Additionally we add a root_event_id to the events, as an equivalent to a trace ID
in opentelemetry. This will allow us to query all events that belong together
without even having to join in the closure.

subject: File upload: Switch to File.slice and iterative hashing
message:
File upload: Switch to File.slice and iterative hashing

Javascript ArrayBuffers have a max size of (2^32)-1 bytes, which means that our max file size would be around 4.3GBs.
Changing to use File.slice instead of going via a buffer that we then slice means that we are not limited to that anymore.

Additionally we introduce hash-wasm to allow for iterative hashing instead of hashing the full object when all is done.
This will allow us, at a later point, to not do all of the upfront work to start passing in the file parts.

subject: Refresh customer portal UI after changes (#8014)
message:
Refresh customer portal UI after changes (#8014)

Fixes #8007

The Customer Portal UI was not updating automatically after subscription
changes (plan changes, cancellations, uncancellations, billing updates,
and payment method changes) because it uses server-side data fetching
with Next.js Server Components.

While the mutations correctly invalidated React Query caches and called
revalidate('customer_portal') to invalidate the Next.js cache, the
client components didn't know to refresh and fetch the updated data.

Solution: Added router.refresh() after successful mutations in:
- CustomerChangePlanModal: After changing subscription plan
- CustomerCancellationModal: After canceling subscription
- CustomerSubscriptionDetails: After uncanceling subscription
- CustomerPortalSettings: After updating billing details or payment methods
- CustomerPortalSubscriptions: After retrying payment

This forces Next.js to refetch server component data, ensuring the UI
updates immediately without requiring a manual page refresh.

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Fix: Trigger customer webhooks when payment method is deleted
message:
Fix: Trigger customer webhooks when payment method is deleted

This fixes issue #7334 where customer.updated and customer.state_changed
webhook events were not being triggered when customers deleted payment
methods from the customer portal.

Previously, adding a payment method correctly triggered webhooks by
updating the customer record through CustomerRepository.update(). However,
deleting a payment method only soft-deleted the payment method without
updating the customer record, so no webhooks were enqueued.

The fix ensures that after deleting a payment method, we explicitly call
CustomerRepository.update() to trigger the webhook events, maintaining
consistency with the add payment method flow.

subject: Spread bulk job enqueuing (#8343)
message:
Spread bulk job enqueuing (#8343)

* Add bulk job spreading for product benefit grant updates

When merchants add new benefits to products with many existing customers,
this prevents queue saturation by spreading job enqueuing over time.

- Add BULK_JOBS_SPREAD_* settings (threshold: 50, min delay: 200ms, max spread: 5min)
- Extend enqueue_job to accept optional delay parameter (ms)
- Add calculate_bulk_job_delay helper to compute staggered delays
- Update order and subscription services to use spreading in update_product_benefits_grants

The spreading logic uses minimum delay (200ms) per job when count is manageable,
but compresses delays to fit within max spread time for very large batches.

* Add minimum delay floor for very large bulk job batches

When batch size exceeds ~6000 items, enforce 50ms minimum delay rather
than using sub-50ms delays which would be meaningless. This means very
large batches may exceed the 5-minute max spread, but each job has a
meaningful delay.

- Rename MIN_DELAY_MS to TARGET_DELAY_MS (200ms target)
- Add new MIN_DELAY_MS as 50ms floor
- Update calculate_bulk_job_delay to enforce the floor

* Export calculate_bulk_job_delay from polar.worker

* Format config.py

* Fix static analysis

matching events.

- Removing `past_due` from revoked_statuses() - now only {canceled, unpaid}
- Adding new `subscription.past_due` webhook event for recoverable payment failures
- Updating docstrings and webhook logic to reflect the semantic distinction
- Fixing InactiveSubscription exception to return 403 status code

This implements fix for issue #8325.

subject: Optimize benefit grant queuing (#8678)
message:
Optimize benefit grant queuing (#8678)

* perf: optimize benefit grant queue by skipping redundant jobs

When processing benefit grants (e.g., when a product is updated with new
benefits), skip enqueueing jobs for:

1. Benefits that are already granted - no need to re-grant
2. Benefits with errors (BenefitActionRequiredError) - these require
   customer action (like connecting OAuth) and should only retry when
   that action is taken, not on every product update

This significantly reduces queue pressure for merchants with large
customer bases and many benefits per product. For example, a product
with 92 benefits and 516 customers previously queued 47,472 jobs on
every product update; now it only queues jobs for new/changed benefits.

Also optimizes revoke task to only process benefits that are actually
granted, avoiding unnecessary revoke attempts.

* fix: only skip BenefitActionRequiredError on grant retry

Only skip retrying grants that specifically failed with
BenefitActionRequiredError, not all errors. Other error types
(e.g., transient network errors) should still be retried on
product updates.

* chore: remove unused Literal import

* refactor: use BenefitActionRequiredError.__name__ instead of hardcoded string

---------

subject: Implement spreading for `meter.billing_entries` (#8687)
message:
Implement spreading for `meter.billing_entries` (#8687)

* Refactor bulk job delay calculation to factory pattern

Replace calculate_bulk_job_delay with make_bulk_job_delay_calculator
that returns a closure, allowing settings to be passed as parameters
instead of using global config. This enables different configurations
for different use cases.

- Remove BULK_JOBS_SPREAD_* constants from config.py
- Use constant values as defaults for factory function parameters
- Update order and subscription services to use new factory pattern

* Add allow_spill parameter to bulk job delay calculator

When allow_spill=True (default), the calculator respects min_delay even
if the total spread time exceeds max_spread. When allow_spill=False,
items are batched together to stay within max_spread while still
respecting min_delay between batches.

* Fix batching to always apply delay including first batch

In the batching case (allow_spill=False), all items now receive a delay
starting from min_delay_ms. For example with items_per_slot=2:
- Items 0-1: delay = min_delay_ms
- Items 2-3: delay = 2 * min_delay_ms
- etc.

* Distribute batched items evenly across all available slots

Instead of using ceil() which may leave slots unused, distribute items
evenly with extra items going to earlier batches.

Example: 15 items over 4 slots = 4-4-4-3 (not 5-5-5-0)

* Spread meter billing jobs over 3 minutes with batching

Use make_bulk_job_delay_calculator with allow_spill=False to ensure
all meter billing jobs are spread over a maximum of 3 minutes, batching
items together when needed to stay within the time limit.

* Unify delay calculation to return None for zero delay

- Make batching zero-based (slot 0 has no delay, like other strategies)
- Replace index == 0 check with delay or None for consistency
- All strategies now return None when calculated delay is 0

* Refactor delay calculator with early returns

- Extract linear_calculator helper for the common delay pattern
- Use early returns for each case instead of nested else blocks
- Cleaner flow: threshold → target → compressed → spill → batch

* Remove threshold from bulk job delay calculator

Removing the threshold ensures spreading logic is exercised in all
environments (dev/test/staging), not just production with large
datasets. This helps catch bugs earlier.

* Self-document code

subject: Disable failing webhooks faster (#8690)

Disable failing webhooks faster (#8690)

* Fix webhook auto-disable not triggering due to pending events

The get_recent_by_endpoint query was returning all recent events including
those with succeeded=NULL (pending/retrying). This caused the auto-disable
check to fail because `all(event.succeeded is False ...)` would return False
when any pending events were in the result set.

Now the query filters to only include completed events (succeeded IS NOT NULL),
so pending events don't block the auto-disable logic from triggering.

* Mark pending webhook events as skipped when endpoint is auto-disabled

When an endpoint is disabled due to consecutive failures, any pending events
(still being retried) are now marked as skipped. This prevents unnecessary
retry attempts and cleans up the event queue immediately.

* test(meter): Add regression test for non-summable aggregation total

Add test_interval_non_summable_aggregation to verify that the `total`
field in MeterQuantities is computed correctly for non-summable
aggregations (max, min) across multiple days.

This test exposes a regression introduced in commit 668ea64 where the
total was always computed using SUM, even for meters configured with
MAX, MIN, or other non-summable aggregations.

Example of the bug:
- Meter with MAX aggregation over 3 days
- Day 1: max = 20, Day 2: none = 0, Day 3: max = 15
- Expected total: max(20, 0, 15) = 20
- Actual (buggy) total: sum(20 + 0 + 15) = 35

* fix(meter): Use correct aggregation function for quantities total

Fix regression introduced in commit 668ea64 where the `total` field in
MeterQuantities was always computed using SUM, even for meters
configured with non-summable aggregations like MAX or MIN.

The fix determines the appropriate SQL window function based on whether
the meter's aggregation is summable:
- For summable aggregations (count, sum): continue using func.sum
- For non-summable aggregations (max, min): use the meter's aggregation
  function (e.g., func.max for MAX aggregation)

Example of the bug this fixes:
- Meter with MAX aggregation tracking "total_enabled_servers"
- Daily values over 30 days: each day reports max of 1
- Expected total: max(1, 1, ..., 1) = 1
- Buggy total: sum(1 + 1 + ... + 1) = 30

Note: avg and unique aggregations require special handling (weighted
averages and deduplication respectively) that is not addressed here.

subject: server/worker: handle max threshold execution debouncing
message:
server/worker: handle max threshold execution debouncing

Problem
-------

The debounce middleware has a max threshold mechanism to ensure tasks eventually execute even when continuously enqueued. However, there was a flaw when a backlog of tasks existed with no new enqueues:

1. Tasks A, B, C, D are enqueued rapidly. D becomes the owner (most recent), but all share the same `enqueue_timestamp` (T0).
2. No more tasks are enqueued.
3. Task A processes first. It's not the owner, but `T0 + max_threshold < now`, so it executes via max threshold.
4. After execution, A deletes the debounce key.
5. Tasks B, C, D process and find no key (`debounce_data` is empty), so they all execute.

Result: 4 executions instead of 2 (max threshold + owner).

Solution
--------

When a task executes via max threshold (non-owner):

1. Mark the execution with `debounce_max_threshold_execution` flag in message options.
2. In `after_process_message`, instead of deleting the key:
   - Reset `enqueue_timestamp` to now (so other non-owners see a fresh timestamp and skip)
   - Refresh the TTL
   - Keep the key so the owner can still execute

Only the owner deletes the key after execution.

Expected behavior after fix
---------------------------

- **A**: not owner, max threshold reached → executes, resets timestamp to T1
- **B**: not owner, `T1 + max_threshold` not reached → skips
- **C**: not owner, same → skips
- **D**: owner → executes, deletes key

Result: 2 executions (A via max threshold, D as owner). B and C correctly skip.

subject: server/worker: improve debounce logic to account for exception and unordered execution
message:
server/worker: improve debounce logic to account for exception and unordered execution

Problem 1: Parallel processing race condition
---------------------------------------------

With multiple workers, there's a small chance that the owner (D) could be processed before earlier tasks (A, B, C), especially if D fails quickly with an exception. When D completes and deletes the key, the remaining tasks find no key and all execute.

Problem 2: Retries not working correctly
----------------------------------------

When a task fails with an exception:
1. The key is deleted in `after_process_message`
2. Dramatiq schedules a retry
3. The retry finds no key and executes without debounce tracking

If other tasks are still pending, they would also execute since the key is gone.

Solution
--------

Replace key deletion with a `debounce_executed` flag:

1. **On enqueue**: Set `debounce_executed = 0` to mark the debounce window as active
2. **Before processing**: If `debounce_executed = 1`, skip (someone already completed the work)
3. **After successful processing**: Set `debounce_executed = 1` instead of deleting the key
4. **On exception**: Do nothing - key remains unchanged, allowing retries to work
5. **On max threshold execution**: Bump timestamp only (existing behavior), don't set executed flag so owner can still run

The key is now cleaned up by TTL (1 hour) rather than explicit deletion.

- **Parallel processing**: Even if D executes first, A, B, C see `debounce_executed = 1` and skip
- **Retries**: On failure, key persists with D as owner, retry executes correctly
- **New enqueues**: Reset `debounce_executed = 0`, starting a fresh debounce window

subject: server/worker: clear debounce enqueue_time when setting executed flag
message:
server/worker: clear debounce enqueue_time when setting executed flag

Problem
-------

The debounce delay metric was showing values up to 4x the configured max threshold. This was caused by stale `enqueue_timestamp` values persisting across debounce windows.

When a debounced task completed successfully, we set `executed=1` but kept the Redis key with the original `enqueue_timestamp`. When a new task with the same debounce key was enqueued later:

1. `hsetnx` for `enqueue_timestamp` did nothing (field already existed)
2. `executed` was reset to 0, starting a new window
3. But `enqueue_timestamp` still held the value from the previous window

This caused the delay metric (`now - enqueue_timestamp`) to include time from the previous debounce window, resulting in artificially inflated values.

Solution
--------

Delete the `enqueue_timestamp` field when marking the debounce key as executed. This allows `hsetnx` to set a fresh timestamp when a new debounce window starts, ensuring the delay metric accurately reflects the current window only.

subject: server/subscription: fix scheduler race condition
message:
server/subscription: fix scheduler race condition

Our custom scheduler worked like this:

* Fetch the subscriptions to be cycled (`get_due_jobs`)
* For each, execute a function that enqueues the `subscription.cycle` task
* Then, the scheduler executes `remove_job`, which sets `scheduler_locked_at`, so the scheduler doesn't pick it up in the next run.

However, we've seen in the wild that our worker is sometimes so fast that it's able to run the `subscription.cycle` task before the `remove_job` is executed. In this case, the subscription is correctly cycled, but it remains locked forever.

To fix this, we directly enqueue the `subscription.cycle` task from within the `remove_job` method, ensuring that the job is only enqueued after the scheduler has set the lock.

Implement a new POST /customers/{id}/anonymize endpoint to anonymize customer PII for GDPR compliance. This is a separate operation from deletion - anonymization removes identifying data while preserving the customer record and all financial/legal data.

Features:
- Idempotent operation: calling on already-anonymized customer succeeds

- Preserves business names (identified by presence of tax_id)

subject: fix: Plain ticket creation when user email changes (#9163)
message:
fix: Plain ticket creation when user email changes (#9163)

When users change their email, Plain ticket creation was failing with
"customer already exists with the provided external id" error. The issue
occurred because the upsert tried to find by the new email (not found) but
created with the user's ID as external_id (already exists with old email).

Implement a "find first, then upsert" pattern:
1. Try to find customer by current email (handles legacy customers)
2. If not found, upsert with external_id as identifier (finds by ID or creates)
3. This gracefully handles email changes, new users, and legacy records

Add _get_or_create_customer helper method and refactor 4 methods to use it.

subject: Avoid escaping {CHECKOUT_ID} in success URL (#9256)
message:
Avoid escaping {CHECKOUT_ID} in success URL (#9256)

* Fix {CHECKOUT_ID} placeholder being URL-encoded in success URLs

Introduce a SuccessUrl type that preserves the {CHECKOUT_ID} placeholder
without encoding curly braces. The implementation temporarily replaces
{CHECKOUT_ID} with a URL-safe marker before HttpUrl validation, then
restores it afterward.

https://claude.ai/code/session_0137RJhzqT4jxt3v4BBhZudz

* Simplify SuccessUrl to unescape encoded placeholder

Instead of replacing {CHECKOUT_ID} before validation and restoring after,
simply let HttpUrl encode it and then unescape %7BCHECKOUT_ID%7D back to
{CHECKOUT_ID} in an AfterValidator. This avoids any collision risk.

https://claude.ai/code/session_0137RJhzqT4jxt3v4BBhZudz

* Add PlainSerializer to SuccessUrl to preserve unescaped value in model_dump

The AfterValidator correctly unescapes {CHECKOUT_ID} during validation,
but model_dump() was still using HttpUrl's serializer which re-encoded it.
Adding PlainSerializer ensures the unescaped string is preserved when
serializing the model.

* Add data migration to fix encoded {CHECKOUT_ID} placeholders

Replace %7BCHECKOUT_ID%7D with {CHECKOUT_ID} in success_url columns
for both checkout_links and checkouts tables.

* Update http.py

- BenefitGrantService passes member to all strategy calls
- OAuth callback endpoints now accept Members and store OAuth on member or customer appropriately
- Added list_errored_by_member_and_benefit_type to BenefitGrantRepository
- CustomerPortalOAuthAccount auth now accepts Member and Anonymous subjects
- Customer portal benefit grant update validates member OAuth accounts when applicable

All tests pass. Type checking passes. No regressions detected.

message:
feat: enable team ownership transfer via customer portal and admin API (#9379)

Implement atomic ownership transfer that prevents the validation deadlock
that made ownership transfer impossible. The fix allows:

1. **Customer Portal**: Only the current owner can transfer ownership to
   another member via PATCH /v1/customer-portal/members/{id}. The caller
   is automatically demoted to billing_manager when promoting another
   member to owner.

2. **Admin API**: Organization admins can transfer ownership via
   PATCH /v1/members/{id} with allow_ownership_transfer=True.

Both paths atomically demote the existing owner to billing_manager
when promoting a member to owner, maintaining the exactly-one-owner
invariant.

Tests added:
- test_owner_can_transfer_ownership: Verifies owner can promote another
  member to owner and is automatically demoted
- test_billing_manager_cannot_transfer_ownership: Verifies non-owners
  cannot transfer ownership
- test_update_member_can_transfer_ownership: Verifies admin API can

subject: benefits: Revoke benefits immediately on product change
message:
benefits: Revoke benefits immediately on product change

Today we have an issue where a meter reset will happen, and benefit revocation and
benefit grants will happen after the fact. This means that someone might lose credits
if they are granted 100 credits today, the meter resets, they receive 1000 credits and
get the 100 credits removed. This means that they end up with 900 credits.

If we instead revoke the benefits, reset the meters and then grant the benefits they will
end up with the 1000 credits as expected.

We utilise the Dramatiq groups+pipelines to ensure that the benefits are revoked first,
and then the meters are reset and finally the new benefits are enqueued.

subject: Refactor webhook event ordering with dynamic retry delays (#9525)
message:
Refactor webhook event ordering with dynamic retry delays (#9525)

* Update webhook retry logic to use retry_when and count-based delay

Replace max_retries with Dramatiq's retry_when for webhook event
sending. NotLatestEvent exceptions (event ordering) always retry with
a delay of count * 500ms. HTTP errors retry up to WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES.
Move is_latest_event query to repository as count_earlier_pending.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Fix retry count by counting delivery attempts instead of shared retries counter

The Dramatiq retries counter is shared between NotLatestEvent retries
and HTTP error retries, so NotLatestEvent waits would inflate the count
and cause premature permanent failures. Count WebhookDelivery records
instead, which only exist for actual HTTP attempts.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Use DeliveryFailed(Retry) for HTTP error retries for readability

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Compute delivery backoff from attempt count, not Dramatiq retries

Dramatiq's Retries middleware uses a global `retries` counter that
includes both DeliveryFailed and NotLatestEvent retries when computing
exponential backoff. This means interleaved ordering retries would
inflate the backoff delay for actual HTTP delivery failures.

Fix by computing the delay ourselves using `delivery_count` (actual
HTTP attempts) and passing it explicitly via `DeliveryFailed(delay=...)`,
which Dramatiq honours directly without its own backoff calculation.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Replace retry_when with computed max_retries for webhook actors

Instead of using retry_when (which bypasses max_retries entirely),
compute a safe upper bound: ordering retries (age_limit / delay) +
delivery retries (WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES). With defaults this is
60s*1000/500 + 10 = 130 retries.

This makes max_retries a proper safety guard while actual HTTP delivery
attempts are still capped by the delivery_count check in the code.

Also extracts hardcoded values into settings:
- WEBHOOK_NOT_LATEST_DELAY_MILLISECONDS (500ms)
- WEBHOOK_ORDERING_AGE_LIMIT (1 minute)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Fix mypy: use self.session instead of self._session

RepositoryBase exposes the session as `self.session`, not `self._session`.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Remove NotLatestEvent/DeliveryFailed subclasses, use plain Retry

These subclasses were only needed to distinguish exception types in
retry_when. Now that we use a computed max_retries and pass explicit
delays on every Retry, the plain Retry class is sufficient.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01QZ966uN86eCkfhDtctRxpi

* Fix tests

* Retry ordering a bit quicker

* Remove temporary, now obsolete `webhook_event.send.v2`

* Rename settings to `FIFO_GUARD`

subject: Ensure zero-decimal currencies payouts are divisible by 100 (#9257)
message:
Ensure zero-decimal currencies payouts are divisible by 100 (#9257)

* Add validation for zero-decimal currencies in Stripe payouts

For currencies like ISK, HUF, TWD, and UGX, Stripe treats them as
zero-decimal currencies for payouts even though they technically have
smaller units. This means payout amounts must be in whole units.

This change:
- Adds STRIPE_PAYOUT_ZERO_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES constant and helper
  functions to polar.kit.currency
- Modifies trigger_stripe_payout() to automatically round down amounts
  to valid values (multiples of 100 in internal representation)
- Updates the payout record with the adjusted amount
- Skips payouts that would round to zero
- Adds comprehensive tests for the new functionality

The remainder from rounding stays in the Stripe Connect account balance
and will be included in the next payout.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XzpQPsp8GSuwoA3rZPH2nF

* Add zero-decimal currency info to payout estimate for frontend warnings

The PayoutEstimate now includes fields to help the frontend warn merchants
about zero-decimal payout currencies (ISK, HUF, TWD, UGX):

- is_zero_decimal_payout_currency: bool indicating if rounding may occur
- adjusted_net_amount: the actual amount that will be paid out (if different)
- unpayable_remainder: the amount that won't be paid this time (0-99)

This allows the frontend to:
- Display a warning for these currencies explaining the rounding
- Show the actual payout amount vs the theoretical net amount
- Explain that the remainder stays in the balance for the next payout

Only populated when there's actually a remainder; otherwise these fields
are null to avoid cluttering the response for exact amounts.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XzpQPsp8GSuwoA3rZPH2nF

* Simplify: net_amount in estimate is now the actual payable amount

Instead of adding multiple fields for zero-decimal currency handling,
just have net_amount reflect the actual amount that will be paid out.
The adjustment function is applied transparently - for regular currencies
it's a no-op, for ISK/HUF/TWD/UGX it rounds down to the nearest 100.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XzpQPsp8GSuwoA3rZPH2nF

* Document zero-decimal currency payout behavior

https://claude.ai/code/session_01XzpQPsp8GSuwoA3rZPH2nF

* Move zero-decimal currency logic to payout/service.py

Consolidate the payout-specific zero-decimal currency handling into the
payout service module instead of keeping it in kit/currency.py. This
keeps the logic closer to where it's used.

Also removes the TestIsPayoutZeroDecimalCurrency test as requested.

* feat: add AI-driven website collector for organization reviews

Add a Playwright-based website scraper with an AI agent that autonomously
explores organization websites to gather compliance review data. The agent
uses three browser tools to navigate, extract content, and gather navigation
links, then produces a structured summary covering business description,
products & pricing, target audience, and red flags.

## Changes

- New `collectors/website.py` with `collect_website_data()` that launches
  a Playwright browser and runs a pydantic_ai agent with browser tools
- Agent tools: `visit_page()` merges navigate + content extraction + link
  gathering into one efficient tool call
- Module-level singleton agent reuses across calls for cost efficiency
- `schemas.py` adds `WebsitePage` and `WebsiteData` with AI-generated
  `summary` field for compliance analysis
- `agent.py` calls `collect_website_data()` after account collection,
  gracefully degrading if scraping fails
- `analyzer.py` includes website summary in the review prompt under
  Product Legitimacy section for cross-reference validation
- `startup.sh` installs Playwright browsers on worker startup for dev

## Design notes

- Single merged `visit_page()` tool cuts LLM round-trips by ~50%
- `retries=0` prevents unnecessary retry loops
- Singleton agent avoids repeated initialization overhead
- Non-fatal collection: website errors don't block reviews
- 90s overall timeout with per-page limits for production resilience

Add debouncing to customer webhook task (#9611)

* Add debouncing to customer.webhook job

Apply the existing DebounceMiddleware to the customer.webhook actor
with a 1 second minimum debounce threshold and 5 second maximum
debounce threshold. The debounce key is scoped to (event_type, customer_id)
so rapid webhook dispatches for the same customer and event type are
coalesced, while different event types still fire independently.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013QE2mSwUmuyiziE7eXFyTp

* Allow debounce_key factory to return None to skip debouncing

Update set_debounce_key to handle None return from the debounce_key
factory function, treating it as an opt-out that queues the message
immediately without debouncing.

Use this in _customer_webhook_debounce_key to only debounce
customer_state_changed events (the high-frequency ones from benefit
grants, subscriptions, and meter updates) while letting
customer_created, customer_updated, and customer_deleted fire
immediately.

* Add tests for set_debounce_key with None factory return

Three test cases for the debounce opt-out behavior:
- Actor with no debounce_key option: returns None, no Redis calls
- Factory returns None: returns None, no Redis calls (new behavior)
- Factory returns a key: sets Redis state and returns (key, delay)

tf: Read the remote state for Render service image

Since we are running into an issue where the digest tracked in Terraform
is not the same as the remote state, we get an error that we cant update it.

Ignoring changes to these fields didn't make a difference since the Render
terraform provider is passing the entire object to Render.

The solution here is to bring in the services as a data source and get
the current image digest for them. This will prevent terraform from
accidentally rolling back a deploy, and hopefully also prevent
the issue we were seeing.

This does, however, introduce a race condition in wich we need to have
the services set up to be able to read them in a data resource.
The solution is simply to comment out the data blocks the first time
we run this, on initial setup.

subject: Skip dunning retries on non-recoverable payment declines (#9744)
message:
Skip dunning retries on non-recoverable payment declines (#9744)

* Skip dunning retries for non-recoverable Stripe decline codes

When a subscription payment fails with a non-recoverable Stripe decline
code (e.g., stolen_card, lost_card, expired_card, do_not_honor), mark
the subscription as past_due but don't schedule automatic dunning
retries. The customer can still manually update their payment method
and retry via the customer portal.

Changes:
- Add decline_code column to Payment model to capture granular Stripe
  decline codes (e.g., stolen_card) separately from error codes
- Capture decline_code from Stripe PaymentIntent.last_payment_error and
  Charge.failure_code in payment service
- Define UNRECOVERABLE_STRIPE_ERROR_CODES and
  UNRECOVERABLE_STRIPE_DECLINE_CODES sets in order service
- Add _is_non_recoverable_decline() check in handle_payment_failure()
  to short-circuit the dunning cycle for permanent failures
- Expose decline_code in the Payment API schema

https://claude.ai/code/session_014j4V7T4hrL8tm2ioXfAXEi

* fix: simplify mid-dunning test to avoid timestamp ordering ambiguity

With freeze_time, multiple payments created at the same frozen timestamp
have non-deterministic ordering from get_latest_for_order. Simplify the
test to use a single non-recoverable payment, which is sufficient to
verify the mid-dunning short-circuit behavior.

https://claude.ai/code/session_014j4V7T4hrL8tm2ioXfAXEi

* style: fix import ordering in order service

https://claude.ai/code/session_014j4V7T4hrL8tm2ioXfAXEi

* simplify: use decline_reason directly instead of adding decline_code column

The decline_reason field already stores the granular Stripe decline codes
(e.g., stolen_card, expired_card, do_not_honor) — no new column needed.

- Remove decline_code from Payment model, schema, service, and migration
- Merge UNRECOVERABLE_STRIPE_ERROR_CODES and UNRECOVERABLE_STRIPE_DECLINE_CODES
  into a single UNRECOVERABLE_DECLINE_CODES set checked against decline_reason
- Simplify _is_non_recoverable_decline to check only decline_reason
- Update tests to set decline_reason directly

https://claude.ai/code/session_014j4V7T4hrL8tm2ioXfAXEi

* Add more unrecoverable Stripe decline codes to skip dunning

Based on production decline data, adds 9 codes that indicate
permanently failed payment methods where automatic retries are futile:
incorrect_number, incorrect_cvc, invalid_cvc, invalid_expiry_year,
invalid_pin, live_mode_test_card, not_permitted, stop_payment_order,
and previously_declined_do_not_retry.

fix: handle duplicate benefit grants in member backfill (#9806)

When the benefit lifecycle creates a new member-linked grant (e.g. during
subscription cancellation) after an org is migrated to the member model,
the old pre-migration grant (member_id=NULL) is left behind. The repair
script then tries to link it to the same member, violating the
benefit_grants_smb_key unique constraint.

Fix: before assigning member_id, check if a member-linked grant already
exists for the same (subscription_id, member_id, benefit_id). If so,
soft-delete the stale unlinked grant and carry over its properties to
the existing grant if needed (e.g. file refs, license keys).

subject: fix:  implicit reverse relationship in organization agent reviews (#9936)
message:
fix:  implicit reverse relationship in organization agent reviews (#9936)

* fix: resolve greenlet async context error in organization agent reviews

The OrganizationAgentReview.organization relationship was defined without
back_populates, allowing SQLAlchemy to create an implicit reverse relationship
with lazy="select". This caused synchronous lazy-load queries when the reverse
side was accessed in async contexts, resulting in "greenlet_spawn has not been
called" errors.

Add explicit bidirectional relationship configuration with lazy="raise" to
prevent accidental lazy-loads and provide clear error messages if the reverse
relationship is accessed without eager loading.

so sub_state provides started_at for all subscriptions referenced by

subject: tinybird: Default to waiting for completion
message:
tinybird: Default to waiting for completion

Since we are relying on our events, we need to ensure that they are saved.

With wait=false, the request returns a 202 response. This means the data has been processed by the ingestion pipeline and will be sent to the database eventually, but the write has not yet been acknowledged by ClickHouse.
With wait=true, the request waits until the database acknowledges the write and returns 200 only once the data has been successfully inserted.

If something fails after the 202 response (for example while writing to the database), the client has no visibility of that failure. With wait=true, the request would instead return an error, which would allow the event.ingested (or other callers) to be retried.

When a customer is deleted, customer_service.delete() soft-deletes all
members synchronously, then enqueues subscription.cancel_customer which
eventually triggers benefit.revoke tasks. By the time benefit.revoke
runs, the owner member is already soft-deleted, but resolve_member()
filtered it out with Member.is_deleted.is_(False).

Add include_deleted param to get_owner_by_customer_id and resolve_member,
and pass True from benefit_revoke. This finds the existing soft-deleted
owner member instead of trying to auto-create a new one.

Fixes SERVER-461

subject: postgres: Disable prepared statement cache
message:
postgres: Disable prepared statement cache

In the hopes that what we are seeing in terms of memory usage is this:
1. SQLAlchemy query cache (engine-level, 1 per engine)
- LRU, 500 entries
- Caches compiled SQL by query shape
- When evicted, compiled objects SHOULD be freed by GC

2. SQLAlchemy asyncpg adapter prepared statement cache (per connection, 100 entries)
- LRU, 100 per connection × 20 pool connections = 2,000 entries
- Caches by SQL string → prepared statement mapping
- Holds references to compiled result column metadata (ResultColumnsEntry, _ColumnsPlusNames, etc.)

3. asyncpg's own prepared statement cache (per connection, 100 entries)
- LRU, 100 per connection × 20 pool connections = 2,000 entries
- Caches by SQL string → PostgreSQL prepared statement handle
- Holds asyncpg.types.Type and asyncpg.types.Attribute for result type descriptions

Request comes in
→ SQLAlchemy compiles query (cache #1 stores compiled objects)
→ SA asyncpg adapter prepares statement (cache #2 references compiled objects)
→ asyncpg sends PREPARE to PostgreSQL (cache #3 stores type info)

SQLAlchemy LRU evicts old query from cache #1
→ compiled objects should be freed...
→ BUT cache #2 still holds a reference to them
→ so they stay alive

subject: logfire: Disable inspect_arguments
message:
logfire: Disable inspect_arguments

Logfire's inspect_arguments feature (enabled by default on Python 3.11+) inspects the caller's stack frame and parses the source AST on every span creation to resolve f-string variables.

  Memray profiling showed this was the single largest allocator: 20.5 GB of allocations across 80k requests, all from ast.parse(). The allocations are short-lived but the volume causes memory fragmentation — RSS grows
  even though the objects are freed.

  With inspect_arguments=False:
  - RSS stays flat at 671 MB (vs 850+ MB growing to 1000+)
  - Throughput improves from 445 to 726 req/s for an arbitrary request that returns 401
  - All observability (spans, traces, scrubbing, attributes) is preserved
  - The only loss is automatic f-string variable resolution, which we don't use

subject: server: Fix race condition in billing entry order creation
message:
server: Fix race condition in billing entry order creation

Prevent double-billing when concurrent order creation tasks read the same
subscription's pending billing entries.

## Problem

The create_order_items_from_pending context manager had a read-then-update
pattern with no locking:

1. READ - Query pending entries (WHERE order_item_id IS NULL)
2. YIELD - Caller creates Order with those items
3. UPDATE - Set order_item_id (WHERE order_item_id IS NULL check)

Two concurrent tasks (e.g., from Dramatiq retry or subscription update racing
with cycle) would both read the same entries at step 1, both create orders at
step 2, and by the time step 3 ran, the second transaction's UPDATE would find
0 matching rows—but the duplicate order was already created.

## Solution

Acquire SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks on all pending billing entries at the
start of create_order_items_from_pending, before any reads. The lock is held
until transaction commit.

With PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED isolation:
- T1 locks entries → reads/processes → creates order → updates entries → commits
- T2 blocks on lock → T1 commits → T2 acquires lock → WHERE re-evaluates → 0 entries → NoPendingBillingEntries raised

Follows existing pattern used in checkout, discount, and customer_meter modules.

subject: payment: Handle Stripe webhook coming before order is stored
message:
payment: Handle Stripe webhook coming before order is stored

If the order is saved (INSERTed) — but the transaction hasn't committed, we will not be able to handle
the charge.succeeded webhook from Stripe, and in that case the order will linger forever in a pending state.

This happens according to the following:
1. INSERT order (saved to DB, but inside an open transaction)
2. Call Stripe API to create payment intent (Stripe charges the card)
3. Stripe sends charge.succeeded webhook to our server
4. Worker picks up the webhook in a separate transaction — can't see the uncommitted order
5. ...more DB work in the PATCH request...
6. PATCH request finishes, transaction commits — order is now visible

By removing the sync guard, we raise the OrderDoesNotExist exception which will
retry the webhook until the order has been written and is available.

subject: payment: Distinguish failed sync payments from uncommitted orders
message:
payment: Distinguish failed sync payments from uncommitted orders

When a sync payment (subscription update) fails, the transaction rolls
back and the order is never committed.
Stripe still sends a webhook, and resolve_order can't find the order.

We removed a blanket guard that returned None for all sync payments
to prevent silently dropped webhooks for *successful* payments
where the transaction just hadn't committed yet.

Now we mark the payment intent with metadata on failure, so the webhook
side can tell the difference:
- No flag → order is coming, keep retrying
- Flag present → order was discarded, exit cleanly

subject: feat: improve denial precision and trust prior human approvals (#10821)
message:
feat: improve denial precision and trust prior human approvals (#10821)

* organization_review: improve denial precision and trust prior human approvals

The agent had a 67% override rate on denials reviewed by humans, with
threshold context being the worst offender (80% override rate, 133 false
denials). Production data showed three dominant root causes:

1. Statistical noise on small payment volumes (e.g. "50% refund rate" on
   2 payments triggering HIGH financial risk).
2. Website-as-primary-evidence at threshold, where the agent re-flags
   services/agency websites despite the org selling digital products on
   Polar and already processing real payments.
3. Re-flagging concerns the human reviewer already considered. One org
   was denied 4 times for the same Lovable cross-domain redirect, despite
   4 prior human approvals tagged "hackathon participant".

Changes:

- Add minimum-volume requirement (10+ payments) for rate-based financial
  thresholds in the system prompt and inject a "LOW VOLUME" warning into
  the rendered metrics block.
- Deweight website content in THRESHOLD_PREAMBLE: treat it as supporting
  context, do not re-raise unchanged website concerns, do not flag an
  unavailable website on its own when the org is already taking payments.
- Strong "trust prior human approval" guidance in THRESHOLD_PREAMBLE and
  MANUAL_PREAMBLE: when a human has already approved, default to APPROVE
  unless there is NEW evidence of a prohibited business or NEW critical
  fraud signals.
- Surface human approvals at the top of the "Prior Review Decisions"
  data block with the count, so the trust signal is impossible to miss.
- Add 6 few-shot APPROVE examples drawn from real false-denial patterns:
  design agency selling templates, AI text humanizer, testimonial SaaS,
  open source pay-what-you-want, low-volume high refund rate, finance
  calculator. Brings APPROVE:DENY ratio to 8:3 (was 2:3).
- Add Lovable domains (lovable.dev, lovable.app, lovableproject.com) to
  the known-domains list so cross-domain redirects between Lovable
  subdomains stop being flagged as scam patterns.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

The previous commit accidentally dropped the default "do not re-raise"
guidance for the no-prior-human-approval branch when refactoring the
prompt builder. Restore it as an else branch and update the test to
cover both branches (with and without a prior human approval).

subject: fix: exclude customer-initiated retries from dunning ceiling (#10857)
message:
fix: exclude customer-initiated retries from dunning ceiling (#10857)

* fix: exclude customer-initiated retries from dunning ceiling

The dunning ceiling counts failed payments to decide when to revoke a
subscription. Previously every failed Payment row counted, so customer-
initiated retries from the portal and one-shot recovery attempts after a
payment-method update inflated the count and could revoke a subscription
within an hour of the first failure instead of over the intended 21-day
dunning window.

This adds a `DUNNING_COUNTING_TRIGGERS` set on the Payment model and uses
it as the single source of truth for both:

- `count_failed_payments_for_order` — only counts failures whose trigger
  is in the set (`purchase` and `retry_dunning`).
- `handle_failure`'s `skip_dunning` derivation — failures from triggers
  outside the set don't progress the dunning state machine either, so a
  one-shot recovery attempt can't push `next_payment_attempt_at` around
  without ever being recorded as a real attempt.

Also extracts the `payment_trigger` Stripe metadata key into a single
`STRIPE_METADATA_PAYMENT_TRIGGER` constant so producers and consumers
can't drift, and drops the legacy `manual_retry: "true"` metadata flag
that the new trigger now subsumes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: enforce exhaustive PaymentTrigger classification

Add a complementary DUNNING_NON_COUNTING_TRIGGERS set and a test that
fails if any PaymentTrigger value is not classified as either counting
or non-counting toward the dunning ceiling. This forces a deliberate
decision when a new trigger is added — silent default to "not counted"
is what created the original bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix: prevent stale Redis messages from corrupting E2E test sessions (#10970)
message:
fix: prevent stale Redis messages from corrupting E2E test sessions (#10970)

Two interacting bugs caused flaky E2E test failures:

1. `group().run()` in `enqueue_benefits_grants` writes directly to the
   real Redis broker, bypassing the drain's FakeRedis. Leftover messages
   from previous test runs or parallel pytest-xdist workers were siphoned
   into unrelated tests, introducing unexpected task failures.

2. When a task fails, `AsyncSessionMaker` calls `session.rollback()` which
   can corrupt the shared test session, causing all subsequent tasks in the
   same drain to fail with "does not exist" errors.

Fix by:
- Purging stale messages from the broker's real Redis at the start of
  each drain, before the current test's JQM is flushed.
- Wrapping each task execution in an explicit SAVEPOINT so that rollbacks
  from failed tasks are isolated and cannot corrupt the outer transaction.

message:
fix(org): unblock Customer Portal settings toggles for legacy orgs (#11034)

* fix(org): make customer_portal allow_email_change NotRequired

Fixes a 422 that blocked any Customer Portal settings toggle (e.g.
"Enable subscription seat management") for orgs created before #10678.

#10678 added customer.allow_email_change to the customer_portal_settings
JSONB without a data migration. Existing orgs' JSONB has no "customer"
key, so react-hook-form's <FormField name="customer.allow_email_change">
registers an undefined path. On any toggle, form.getValues() serializes
customer as {} (undefined values stripped by JSON), and Pydantic rejects
because allow_email_change was a required bool.

The read paths already tolerate a missing key
(customer_email_update.py uses .get("allow_email_change", False)), so
aligning the TypedDict with the defensive reads unblocks every caller
(UI + API/SDK) without a data migration.

Logfire shows ~14k failed PATCH /v1/organizations/{id} across 18 orgs
in the past 7 days (sandbox + production) driven by auto-save retries.

Add regression tests for PATCH /v1/organizations/{id} covering:
- customer_portal_settings without "customer" key (legacy org shape)
- customer_portal_settings with empty customer: {} (rhf-serialized
  payload when the field is registered but never set — this was the
  original 422 trigger)
- customer_portal_settings with full customer: {allow_email_change: true}

`meter.create_billing_entries` now skips events that fall within the
subscription's trial period, so no billable `BillingEntry` rows exist

subject: fix(settings): stop infinite save loop in Billing settings (#11050)
message:
fix(settings): stop infinite save loop in Billing settings (#11050)

Toggling any switch in Settings → Billing triggered an endless stream
of PATCH /v1/organizations/{id} requests. The useAutoSave hook watched
derived state (isDirty / formValues / a re-created debouncedSave) inside
a useEffect whose deps changed on every render. Combined with the two
revalidate() server actions fired by useUpdateOrganization.onSuccess
(each triggering a Next.js router refresh), the isDirty and isSaving
guards raced and re-scheduled the same save indefinitely.

Switch to a direct form.watch() subscription filtered on
info.type === 'change', so programmatic updates from reset() (fired
after a successful save) cannot re-trigger the loop. Concurrency is
guarded by a ref instead of state, onSave is held in a ref to tolerate
inline definitions in consumers, and the timeout + subscription are
properly cleaned up on unmount.

Dropped the unused isSaving return value (no caller read it) and added
a try/catch around the save call so an unmount mid-save does not
surface as an unhandled rejection.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(seeds): batch Tinybird ingest per org in seeds_load (#11049)

* perf(seeds): batch Tinybird ingest per org to speed up seeds_load

`uv run task seeds_load` was dominated by Tinybird HTTP round-trips:
each customer triggered a separate POST to `/v0/events?wait=true`, and

number of Tinybird calls from O(customers) to O(orgs).

subject: fix(appeal-review): re-check Plain thread state before auto-replying (#11059)
message:
fix(appeal-review): re-check Plain thread state before auto-replying (#11059)

* fix(appeal-review): re-check Plain thread state before auto-replying

The bulk-appeal-review cron filters unanswered appeal threads once at
the start of a run, then processes each sequentially (AI review +
website scrape per org takes minutes). With the job running every 6h
and handling every unanswered appeal, humans who act on a thread mid-run
were getting contradicted by an automated follow-up — one case sent a
follow-up email 15 minutes after the appeal had been approved.

Re-check the thread's Plain status and staff-reply state immediately
before posting the reply, and also check that the DB appeal decision is
still unresolved. Skip with a log line if either changed. The race
window shrinks from hours to the handful of ms between check and send.

Also reuse the existing httpx client (which already carries the Plain
auth header) instead of creating a new one per check.

subject: fix: add authorization checks to prevent customer access (#11070)
message:
fix: add authorization checks to prevent customer access (#11070)

* customer-portal: Reject anonymous callers on OAuth authorize

The customer-portal OAuth authorize endpoint accepted `customer_id` as a
query parameter and, for anonymous callers, encoded it verbatim into a
signed state JWT. The callback then trusted that state's `customer_id`
to look up the customer and mint a customer session token.

This meant any anonymous caller who knew a customer's UUID could call
/authorize with that UUID, complete an OAuth flow with their own
GitHub/Discord account, and get a valid customer session token for the
victim (plus link their OAuth account to the victim's customer). Merchants
typically know their own customers' IDs, and UUIDs also leak through a
number of other surfaces (webhooks, URLs, etc.).

Fix: require the caller to be authenticated (Customer or Member) on the
authorize endpoint and always derive `customer_id` from the subject —
never from the query string. The `customer_id` query parameter is now
unused and has been removed from both the endpoint signature and the
frontend call site.

The callback continues to allow anonymous callers because browsers
follow GitHub/Discord's cross-origin redirect without forwarding our
Authorization header; it's safe because the state JWT it trusts can
only be produced by an authenticated /authorize call.

subject: fix(subscription): atomic claim in scheduler to prevent duplicate cycle tasks (#11065)
message:
fix(subscription): atomic claim in scheduler to prevent duplicate cycle tasks (#11065)

* fix(subscription): atomic claim in scheduler to prevent duplicate cycle tasks

Two scheduler instances (rolling deploy, extra replica, or brief overlap
during restart) could each enqueue `subscription.cycle` for the same
subscription. Logfire shows duplicates with sub-millisecond gaps — the
smoking gun for concurrent processes.

Root cause: `SubscriptionJobStore.get_due_jobs` did a non-atomic read,
and `remove_job` did a separate UPDATE to set `scheduler_locked_at`.
Any overlap between `get_due_jobs` (on instance A) and `remove_job`
(on instance B) let both see `scheduler_locked_at IS NULL` and both
send the dramatiq task.

Fix: claim due subscriptions in a single
`UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING …`
inside `get_due_jobs`. Only one instance's UPDATE wins each row;
`remove_job` then just fires the task.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(subscription): move atomic claim to remove_job to avoid stuck claims

Prior version claimed upfront in ``get_due_jobs`` via
``UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING ...``.
Efficient, but if the scheduler crashed between that batch claim and the
per-job ``remove_job`` enqueues, N rows ended up with ``scheduler_locked_at``
set and no dramatiq message — stuck until manual intervention.

Move the claim to ``remove_job`` itself: a per-subscription conditional
``UPDATE ... WHERE id = :id AND scheduler_locked_at IS NULL`` just before
``actor.send(...)``. Equivalent to a SELECT FOR UPDATE on the single row but
in one statement. Only the instance whose UPDATE flips the NULL proceeds;
losers see 0 rows and bail out.

Trade-off: more per-tick DB writes when instances overlap (each remove_job
does a conditional UPDATE), but the claim window is now one subscription
wide and adjacent to the enqueue, so a mid-tick crash just leaves the row
unclaimed for the next tick to pick up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(subscription): simplify scheduler diff

Post-review cleanup of the atomic-claim fix:
- Use ``.rowcount == 0`` instead of ``.returning(id).first() is None`` to
  detect a losing-race UPDATE, matching the existing pattern in
  ``order/repository.py``.
- Drop the now-redundant ``_build_job`` extraction (single caller).
- Trim the multi-line comment in ``remove_job`` to one line.

No behavior change.

subject: clients/web: fix auto save of organization social links (#11088)
message:
clients/web: fix auto save of organization social links (#11088)

**Problem**

The social media links form wasn't triggering auto-save. The root cause was that the component was using `setValue()` directly to update the form state, but the `useAutoSave` hook only responds to user input changes marked with `info.type === 'change'`. Direct `setValue()` calls are programmatic updates that don't trigger this event type.

**Solution**

Wrapped the social links component in a `FormField` and changed all state updates to use `field.onChange()` instead of `setValue()`:

- **Input changes**: `field.onChange(updatedSocials)` in the text input's `onChange` handler
- **Remove social**: `field.onChange(socials.filter(...))` when clicking the delete button
- **Add social**: `field.onChange([...socials, ...])` when clicking the "Add Social" button

Now every user interaction triggers a proper change event that `useAutoSave` listens for, so the form auto-saves after 1 second of inactivity. Server errors are properly reported via the existing error handling in the `onSave` function.

fix(organization): gate CREATED → ACTIVE on all onboarding checks (#11090)

* fix(organization): gate CREATED → ACTIVE on all onboarding checks

Before the Apr 8 refactor (#10906 / 5fe86daf7), the Stripe account.updated
webhook was responsible for transitioning organizations to ACTIVE once the
payout account was fully set up. That path was removed when Account and
PayoutAccount were split. In its place, the AI review task started flipping
orgs to ACTIVE on APPROVE alone — which skips identity verification and
payout-account readiness.

Introduce OrganizationService.maybe_activate as the single gated transition:
CREATED → ACTIVE only when details are submitted, the AI review verdict is
PASS, the payout account has details/charges/payouts enabled, and the admin
identity is verified. It delegates to confirm_organization_reviewed so the
held-balance release, initially_reviewed_at, threshold doubling, and email
(silent) all run through one path.

Wire it into the three events that can satisfy a gate:
- AI review APPROVE branch (organization_review/tasks.py)
- Stripe account.updated → payout_account.update_account_from_stripe
- identity.verification_session.verified → user.identity_verification_verified

The helper is idempotent, so whichever event completes last triggers the
transition.

Also add scripts/backfill_stuck_active_orgs.py for the ~16 orgs that already
satisfy every gate but are stuck in CREATED due to the Apr 8 regression.

* fix(organization): route appeals through maybe_activate; drop misleading filter

appeal decision and delegates activation to maybe_activate so that
appeal-approved orgs go through the same gates (payout + identity) as fresh
activations. If a gate is still unmet the org stays in its current state and
will activate later when the relevant webhook fires.

confirm_organization_reviewed requires a reason when reactivating from
DENIED or BLOCKED; pass through review.appeal_reason in those cases.

Also drop the `initially_reviewed_at IS NULL` filter from the backfill
predicate. It was redundant (status == CREATED already implies this in
practice since the state machine has no path back to CREATED) and read as

has not completed." maybe_activate re-checks every gate itself, so relying
on it as source of truth is cleaner.

test_approve_appeal_success asserts the status flip to ACTIVE without

subject: fix(paginate): strip projected columns from count subquery and revert blocked_at drop (#11119)
message:
fix(paginate): strip projected columns from count subquery and revert blocked_at drop (#11119)

The paginate() helpers wrapped the caller's ORM entity select in
.subquery() to count rows. SQLAlchemy's deferred=True only controls the
outermost SELECT delivered to the client and does NOT propagate into
columns rendered inside .subquery(), so a column marked deferred on the
model still gets projected in the count subquery. Once the underlying
DB column is dropped, pagination queries fail with UndefinedColumnError
(ref: SERVER-4DP on sandbox after #11105's migration ran).

Changes:

- RepositoryBase.paginate() now projects self.model.id in the count
  subquery. Bounded RepositoryBase on ModelIDProtocol[Any] so .id is
  guaranteed and no type ignore is needed.
- kit/pagination.paginate() helper projects literal(1). Verified no
  caller of this helper uses DISTINCT (the one DISTINCT case routes
  through RepositoryBase where .id is used instead).
- Revert the drop-blocked-at migration from #11105 and restore the
  mapped attribute on Organization. The paginate fix needs to be fully
  rolled out before the column can be dropped safely; re-landing the
  drop as its own PR after this ships avoids the rolling-deploy race.

Refs: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/8838

subject: feat(organization): migrate enforcement reads to capabilities (PR2) (#11104)
message:
feat(organization): migrate enforcement reads to capabilities (PR2) (#11104)

* feat(organization): migrate enforcement reads to capabilities (PR2)

Migrates the six merchant-facing enforcement gates from `Organization.status`
checks to the `capabilities` JSONB column added in PR1. Backoffice admins
can now flip a single capability without inventing new statuses; status
transitions still reset every override.

- Backfill migration: populates `capabilities` from `status` for existing
  rows, mirrors current `refunds_blocked` overrides into the JSONB blob,
  then sets the column NOT NULL.
- New typed hybrid properties on `Organization`: `can_accept_payments`,
  `can_renew_subscriptions`, `can_payout`, `can_refund`. Existing
  `can_authenticate` switched to read `capabilities["api_access"]`; new
  `can_access_dashboard` reads `capabilities["dashboard_access"]`.
- Enforcement migrated: checkout (3 sites), subscription cycle scheduler
  (JSONB SQL filter), order dunning repository + service, payouts, refunds.
- Defensive short-circuits added in `subscription.cycle` and
  `process_dunning_order` for capability flips between scheduler pickup
  and task execution.
- `set_status()` now also keeps the legacy `refunds_blocked` shim in sync
  so the column doesn't drift across status transitions until PR5 drops it.
- Restored `set_status()` routing in `organization/service.py`,
  `organization_review/tasks.py`, and the seed/enable_payments scripts
  (these were temporarily bypassed in PR1's model-only commit).
- Drift guard: a unit test asserts the migration's hardcoded
  `_STATUS_DEFAULTS` matches the model's `STATUS_CAPABILITIES` matrix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fixup: rebase fixes + audit checkout gates + drop migration

- Rebase onto main (resolves conflicts in service/tests for new
  ALLOWED_STATUS_TRANSITIONS validation and refactored review flow)
- Drop the redundant backfill migration: scripts/backfill_org_capabilities.py
  (already in main) is the canonical backfill; column NOT NULL flip will be
  a follow-up PR after the script runs in prod
- Revert capabilities column to nullable=True to match main + DB schema;
  add a private _capability() helper that falls back to STATUS_CAPABILITIES
  for un-backfilled rows
- Audit checkout gates: get_by_id and create early-gate were originally
  is_blocked() (status==BLOCKED → api_access=False), so they belong on
  can_authenticate, not can_accept_payments. The full payment-readiness
  check still happens at /confirm via is_organization_ready_for_payment

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(order): include retry_customer in renewal-payment trigger set

retry_customer is a customer-initiated retry of a failed subscription
renewal — it belongs to the same recurring-billing capability gate as
retry_dunning and retry_payment_method_update.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* simplify: extract get_effective_capabilities + RENEWAL_PAYMENT_TRIGGERS

- Promote the NULL-fallback logic into a public
  ``Organization.get_effective_capabilities()`` so the model and the
  backoffice endpoint stop duplicating the same fallback expression.
- Type ``_capability(name)`` with a ``CapabilityName`` Literal so callers
  get key-name validation at type-check time and the # type: ignore lines
  go away.
- Move the renewal-payment trigger classification into
  ``models/payment.py`` next to the existing dunning sets, where it
  belongs alongside ``DUNNING_(NON_)COUNTING_TRIGGERS``.
- Drop two narrating comments that referenced PR5 / restated the code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(payment): move renewal-payment classification onto PaymentTrigger

Replace the ``RENEWAL_PAYMENT_TRIGGERS`` module-level set with a
``PaymentTrigger.is_renewal_payment()`` method. Same semantics
(``purchase`` is the only non-renewal trigger), but the classification
now lives on the enum so callers don't have to import a separate set.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* simplify(organization): collapse is_organization_ready_for_payment to capability check

The function used to enforce four extra prerequisites (details submitted,
payout account present, payout account ready, admin identity verified)
on top of the status gate. Those prerequisites belong upstream — they
should be enforced before ``capabilities.checkout_payments`` is flipped
on, not at every payment attempt.

The follow-up that moves the ~1.5k orgs whose capability is True without
the prerequisites back to CREATED is tracked separately. Once that lands,
the capability flag is the single source of truth and this function can
remain a one-liner.

Drop the session parameter (no DB load left) and make the function
synchronous. Update the three callers (organization service,
checkout confirm, backoffice setup analytics) and rewrite tests that
previously toggled status without going through ``set_status()``.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* simplify(organization): drop sync/session ceremony around payment-status helpers

- ``get_payment_status`` was async and took a ``session`` it never used —
  make it sync and drop the parameter (one endpoint caller updated).
- Use ``settings.is_sandbox()`` instead of the inline
  ``settings.ENV == Environment.sandbox`` comparison; drop the now-dead
  ``Environment`` import here and in the test.
- Trim the ``is_organization_ready_for_payment`` docstring to the WHY
  (sandbox bypass) and drop the implementation narration.
- Delete redundant ``TestOffboardingPaymentReady`` — the OFFBOARDING ↦
  capability mapping is already covered by
  ``TestSetStatusCapabilities`` and ``TestCapabilityOverrides``.
- Rewrite ``TestGetPaymentStatus`` against the capability gate:
  active-org positive case + sandbox-bypass case. The grandfathering
  test became meaningless once the helper stopped reading
  ``created_at``.
- Simplify the checkout ``test_payment_not_ready_*`` tests — the
  fixture default is ACTIVE, and ACTIVE → BLOCKED is a legal
  transition, so the ``status = X; set_status(Y)`` bypass dance is
  unnecessary.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address review feedback — drop OrgModel alias, propagate capabilities in seeds

- order/repository.py: import Organization directly from polar.models and drop the

- scripts/seeds_load.py: route status assignment through set_status() so seeded
  orgs get capabilities aligned with their status. Previously every active seed org
  ended up with CREATED-default capabilities (checkout_payments=false, etc.),
  which broke local UI testing.

subject: member: prevent duplicate owner when customer email drifts (#11158)
message:
member: prevent duplicate owner when customer email drifts (#11158)

Customers ended up with two active owner members after a customer.email
correction: the pre-existing sync guarded `owner.email == old_email` and
silently no-oped on any drift (punctuation, whitespace, prior un-synced
correction), leaving owner.email stale. The next portal sign-in looked
up the member by the new email, missed the stale owner, and auto-created
a second one. Every subsequent get_owner_by_customer_id call then raised
MultipleResultsFound, surfacing as 500s in the portal and backoffice
"Generate Portal Link".

Centralize the mirror logic in MemberService.sync_owner_email which,
for individual customers, unconditionally rewrites owner.email to match
customer.email. Both update paths (customer_service.update and
customer_email_update.verify) call it instead of their own blocks.

Also switch create_owner_member's dedupe from (customer_id, email) to
get_owner_by_customer_id so the auto-create path reuses the existing
owner even when emails have drifted.

subject: events: Decouple parent and child ingestion (#11149)
message:
events: Decouple parent and child ingestion (#11149)

* events: Decouple parent and child ingestion

This allows us to decouple the ingestion of a child event and its parent. By storing the pending parent id on events,
we can at a later date resolve this relationship. We write the events to postgres always, but we wait with writing
to Tinybird until we have resolved the relationship.

An orphan child will not show up anywhere, although we could have a list of orphan events in the dashboard. This is
intentional as we want to avoid writing and updating data in Tinybird. Especially since we will need to update both the
root_id, as well as the ancestor_chain. If you are ingesting a grand-grand child and then their parent, you will have to ingest
two more events before you complete the chain and can truly know the events full ancestry.

* events: Simplify pending parent resolution

* events: Add pure SQL comment to describe the python

* events: Ensure that a parent in a later batch resolves earlier child

If a child event gets ingested first and then in a later batch the parent comes in
without any other child events, it should still resolve the child's parent id

* events: Add a test with a deeper hierarchy of resolution
