message:
feat(authz): centralized authorization with PolicyGuard (#11126)

* feat(authz): add centralized authorization module with OrgPolicyGuard

Introduce server/polar/authz/ with org-access resolver, policy
functions (finance, organization, members), OrgPolicyGuard FastAPI
dependency factory, and typed Authorize* dependencies.

* refactor(organization): migrate endpoints to PolicyGuard authorization

Replace ad-hoc admin checks in organization endpoints with declarative
Authorize* DI dependencies:

- GET /{id}/account: AuthorizeFinanceRead (was manual is_user_admin check)
- DELETE /{id}: AuthorizeOrgDelete (was inline account admin check in service)
- POST /{id}/members/invite: AuthorizeMembersManage (was OrganizationsWrite)
- DELETE /{id}/members/leave: AuthorizeOrgAccess (was manual get_admin_user)
- DELETE /{id}/members/{user_id}: AuthorizeMembersManage (was manual get_admin_user)

Each endpoint now receives an AuthorizedOrganization from DI containing
both the resolved organization and the auth_subject. Authorization
checks cannot be skipped since they are enforced by the dependency.

Removes the duplicate admin check from OrganizationService.request_deletion
since authorization is now handled at the endpoint layer.

Adds AccountService.get_by_organization for auth-free account lookup
(authorization already handled by PolicyGuard).

* test(authz): add tests for policies, org-access resolver, and PolicyGuard

- test_service: get_accessible_org_ids returns correct org IDs for
  User subjects (with/without orgs) and Organization subjects
- test_policies: policy functions return True for allowed access and
  descriptive denial reason strings for denied access, covering
  finance.can_read, organization.can_delete, and members.can_manage
- test_endpoints: integration tests for PolicyGuard behavior across
  get_account, delete org, invite member, and remove member endpoints
  verifying 401 for anonymous, 404 for non-members, 403 with specific
  messages for unauthorized members, and 200 for authorized access

* docs: add authorization handbook entry

Document how authorization works: PolicyGuard DI dependencies,
policy functions, org-scoped data access, scope model, and how
to add new policy-guarded endpoints.

* fix(authz): type safety and policy correctness

- OrgPolicyGuard return type: Any instead of type (mypy fix)
- AuthorizeOrgAccessUser: User-only variant for leave_organization
  (prevents type confusion with Organization tokens)
- Policies (members, organization): check admin directly instead of
  delegating to finance.can_read — allows any member to manage/delete
  orgs without accounts
- Type guards: add is_user() asserts in delete and invite endpoints
- Test fix: use object.__setattr__ for mypy compatibility

* refactor(authz): extract PolicyResult to types.py and remove wrapper functions

Breaks the circular import between dependencies.py and policies/ by moving
PolicyResult and PolicyFn to a dedicated types module. This allows guards
to reference policy functions directly (e.g. finance.can_read) instead of
through intermediary _finance_can_read() wrappers.

message:
paginate: add count_subquery helper and lint for .subquery() misuse (#11124)

* paginate: add count_subquery helper and lint for .subquery() misuse

Extract the count-subquery projection pattern into a named helper and
add a lint that flags `select(Model).subquery()` without
`.with_only_columns(...)`. This is the same class of bug that caused the
sandbox Organization outage (#11119): `deferred=True` does not propagate
into `.subquery()`, so the count subquery silently materializes every
mapped column — including deferred TSVECTOR/large-string ones, which is
both a performance tax today and a correctness risk when a deferred
column is later dropped at the DB level.

  paginate helpers
- scripts/lint_subquery.py AST walker, wired into `task lint_check`
  (and therefore CI) via a new `lint_subquery` taskipy task

message:
refactor(member): atomic ownership transfer via single CASE-based UPDATE (#11179)

Replaces the two-step demote-then-promote ownership transfer with a single
CASE-based UPDATE via a new `MemberRepository.transfer_ownership` helper.
The repository method also refreshes the in-memory role on both instances
so the webhook payload stays accurate after the raw UPDATE.

This is a prerequisite for the follow-up partial unique index
`members(customer_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND role = 'owner'`:
once that index exists, the previous two-statement transfer would briefly
expose two owners between UPDATEs and trip the constraint.

Also removes two misnamed tests in `test_customer_portal/test_member.py`
whose docstrings claimed they tested "cannot demote/remove only owner" but
whose bodies instead created two owners and asserted that demoting/removing
one succeeded — a scenario the service-level invariant already forbids.
Proper "only owner" coverage is already provided by `test_cannot_modify_self`
and `test_cannot_remove_self` in the same file.

subject: feat(member): partial unique index to enforce one active owner per customer (#11181)
message:
feat(member): partial unique index to enforce one active owner per customer (#11181)

Adds a partial unique index on `members(customer_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
AND role = 'owner'` so the "at most one active owner per customer" invariant
is enforced at the database level instead of relying on application-level
checks. Follow-up to #11158, which handled one class of drift but could not
close the race window at the DB layer.

**Must be deployed AFTER #11179** — that PR refactors the two-statement
ownership transfer into a single CASE-based UPDATE, which is required once
this index exists (otherwise the intermediate state between demote and
promote would briefly expose two owners and trip the constraint).

Migration uses `CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` inside `autocommit_block()`
with `SET lock_timeout = '5s'` for defensive catalog-lock safety. No
`statement_timeout` — killing CONCURRENTLY mid-build would leave an INVALID
index that still enforces uniqueness.

* perf(orders): split product_billing_type filter into two queries

The Product.billing_type hybrid property expands to a CASE expression
over recurring_interval and a product_prices subquery. When attached to
the orders WHERE clause, Postgres cannot push this past the join, forcing
it to evaluate the CASE per candidate row and defeating the ORDER BY
created_at + LIMIT early-termination.

Fetch matching product IDs up front via a new ProductRepository method,
then filter orders on a literal IN list. Short-circuit to an empty page
when no products match the billing type.

Verified on prod: cost drops from 9331 to ~3000 on a large-org query.

* perf(plain): split customer-card order lookup into two queries

The previous single query (WHERE lower(customers.email) = $1 ORDER BY
orders.created_at DESC LIMIT 3) let Postgres plan a reverse index scan
over all 2.8M orders, probing customers row-by-row — cost ~478k even
for emails that match one customer.

Resolve customer IDs up front against the existing ix_customers_email_not_null
partial functional index, then fetch top-3 orders by customer_id IN list.
Short-circuit when no customers match.

Verified on prod: cost drops from ~478k to ~5k (~100x).

fix(organization): skip review-threshold check for ineligible statuses (#11203)

* fix(organization): skip review-threshold check for ineligible statuses

The order-balance worker calls `check_review_threshold` for every org on
the destination account after a balance transfer lands. The existing
early-return only covered `is_under_review` ({REVIEW, SNOOZED}), so orgs
in OFFBOARDING (and any other non-re-reviewable state) fell through to

since transition rules were enforced.

For an OFFBOARDING org with `next_review_threshold = 0`, every balance
transfer poisoned the order.balance Dramatiq message — the transaction
was persisted but the worker kept retrying forever.

Narrow the check to the statuses that actually warrant re-review
(ACTIVE, REVIEW, SNOOZED). Others are left alone; `total_balance` is
still synced from the earlier branch.

subject: fix(member): forbid role=owner on public member create endpoint (#11231)
message:
fix(member): forbid role=owner on public member create endpoint (#11231)

Owners are established when the customer is created (via the optional
`owner` field on `CustomerCreate`) or auto-provisioned on first
interaction, and ownership is transferred via the member update
endpoint. Accepting `role=owner` on `POST /v1/members/` made it
possible for callers to attempt to insert a second active owner,
which the partial unique index `members_customer_id_owner_active_key`
correctly rejects — but the resulting `IntegrityError` was caught in a
way that touched an expired ORM attribute, surfacing to clients as a
`PendingRollbackError` 500 instead of a clean 4xx.

Narrow `MemberCreate.role` to `Literal[member, billing_manager]` so
the request is rejected by Pydantic at the boundary with a 422 and
the database is never touched.

message:
fix(checkout): preserve placeholder for unset optional custom fields (#11246)

When creating a checkout via the Checkout Session API,
`validate_custom_field_data` populated optional unset fields with their
defaults (e.g. `None` for select fields). The frontend then passed those
nulls as the Select's `defaultValue`, which suppressed the
`form_placeholder`. Checkout links did not hit this code path when no
prefill was provided, which is why placeholders worked there.

Use `exclude_unset=True` on `model_dump` so the validated output only
contains fields the caller explicitly provided. Validation of required
fields is unaffected because it happens during `model_validate`.

subject: Add country-specific minimum payout amounts (#11270)
message:
Add country-specific minimum payout amounts (#11270)

* payout: Apply country-based minimum payout amounts

Stripe enforces per-country minimum payout amounts in each recipient's
local currency, but Polar triggers all payouts in USD. We convert each
country's local minimum to USD using current FX rates and round up to
the next multiple of $5 USD to give us headroom against FX fluctuations,
then enforce the larger of the country and currency minimums.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013PFnuei5WneNUKfHyFhXoy

* app: Drop the hardcoded $10 minimum withdrawal label

The minimum is no longer a fixed $10 — it varies by payout currency and
recipient country, so swap the specific figure for the same generic
copy used by the web app.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013PFnuei5WneNUKfHyFhXoy

* Apply suggestion from @pieterbeulque

* payout: Make country required on get_minimum_payout

Both call sites always have a payout account country, so drop the
optional default to make the contract explicit.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013PFnuei5WneNUKfHyFhXoy

* payout: Trim country minimums dominated by per-currency floor

After cross-referencing with the public payouts doc table, the
per-currency minimum already meets or exceeds the Stripe per-country
minimum for every country except three: Bahamas (BSD isn't listed in
the per-currency dict so it falls back to the $10 default), and
El Salvador and Panama (both pay out in USD, where the currency floor
is $10 but Stripe enforces 30 USD and 50 USD respectively).

Drop the redundant entries and document the three exceptions in the
payouts doc.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013PFnuei5WneNUKfHyFhXoy

* Apply suggestion from @pieterbeulque

---------

Adds GET endpoints that return a presigned URL to download an order's
receipt PDF, plus the receipt_number field on the Order schema and a
backoffice link.

- GET /v1/customer-portal/orders/{id}/receipt (auth: customer portal)

order_service.get_order_receipt / customer_order_service.get_order_receipt,
which delegate to receipt_service.get_pdf_url_or_status. A new
ReceiptNotAllocated exception (404) is raised when receipt_number is
unset, mirroring InvoiceDoesNotExist.

Adds the S3_CUSTOMER_RECEIPTS_BUCKET_NAME setting and a receipt_filename
property on Order.

Safe to merge before the render pipeline lands: every prod order has
receipt_number = NULL today (PR3 is gated on Organization.receipts_enabled,
which defaults to false), so all three endpoints return 404 and the
button stays hidden in the customer portal.

subject: auth: split web-user authentication and authorization (#11303)
message:
auth: split web-user authentication and authorization (#11303)

* auth: split web-user authentication and authorization

`WebUserRead` and `WebUserWrite` were identical aliases that conflated
authentication ("must be a web session") with an implied authorization
gradient that didn't exist. Collapse them into `WebUserSession` (pure
authentication) and introduce `AuthorizeWebUser` in `authz/dependencies.py`
as the user-personal analogue of the always-allow `OrgPolicyGuard`
variants — currently policy-free, but the layer where future per-user
checks (suspended account, identity not verified, MFA, …) can be added
without touching endpoint signatures.

Migrate the 11 endpoint files that used the old aliases, and document
the user-personal pattern in the authorization handbook.

* auth: gate user-personal endpoints with explicit scopes

The previous commit collapsed `WebUserRead`/`WebUserWrite` into a single
authentication primitive and added an `AuthorizeWebUser` authorization
layer with no policy. That preserved behavior but kept a 2-day-old gap
opened by #11148: user-personal write endpoints (`PATCH /users/me`,
`DELETE /personal_access_tokens/{id}`, OAuth-link callbacks, …) were
reachable by impersonation sessions because they didn't declare any
required scope.

Replace the single `AuthorizeWebUser` with scope-gated aliases following
the same pattern as `OrgPolicyGuard` variants:

- `AuthorizeUserRead` / `AuthorizeUserWrite`
- `AuthorizePayoutsRead` / `AuthorizePayoutsWrite`
- `AuthorizeOrganizationsRead`

Each endpoint now declares the scope it needs. Impersonation sessions
carry only `READ_ONLY_SCOPES`, so any endpoint requiring a `_write` scope
is automatically off-limits to them — same invariant that already
protects org-scoped resource writes, now extended to user-personal ones.

A few endpoints were previously annotated as writes despite being pure
reads (e.g. `GET .../user/repositories`, `GET .../guild/lookup`); those
flip to the correct read alias.

Update the `user_read`/`user_write` display names to "Read your user
account" / "Manage your user account" — the previous "Delete your user
account" label for `user_write` was misleading now that the scope gates
broader user-account mutations (profile, OAuth links, PATs, email).

* test(auth): cover the impersonation read-only invariant

Add direct contract tests for ``WebUserAuthorizer`` and impersonation
gates on representative endpoints. Without these, the test suite would
have remained blind to the regression class introduced by #11148:
``AuthSubjectFixture`` defaults to ``set(Scope)``, so a missing
``required_scopes`` declaration on a write endpoint is invisible — every
authed test session has every scope.

Three layers of coverage:

1. Unit tests on ``WebUserAuthorizer`` exercise the factory contract
   directly: scope-match passes, missing scope raises, read-aliases
   accept either ``_read`` or ``_write``, write-aliases reject
   ``_read`` only. Includes a sanity check that ``READ_ONLY_SCOPES``
   contains no ``_write`` scopes — if a future addition ever violates
   this, every user-personal write endpoint silently becomes reachable
   by impersonation, so the test fails loudly.

2. Endpoint-level impersonation tests on ``user``, ``feedback``, and
   ``payout_account`` (the modules with existing endpoint tests):
   sessions parameterized with ``READ_ONLY_SCOPES`` are accepted on
   reads (``GET /users/me``, ``GET /payout-accounts/``) and rejected
   with 403 on writes (``PATCH /users/me``, ``POST /feedbacks/``,
   ``POST /payout-accounts/``).

3. Together, (1) verifies the dependency contract and (2) verifies the
   wiring on real endpoints — the two failure modes that would let a
   future change re-open the gap.

* auth: address code-review findings

Three follow-ups from review of the prior commits in this PR:

1. Migrate ``DELETE /users/me`` to ``AuthorizeUserWrite`` and retire
   ``polar/user/auth.py``. The endpoint had been the last consumer of
   the legacy ``UserWrite`` ``Authenticator``, which goes through the
   plain authentication layer with no web-session check — meaning an
   impersonation session could still delete the impersonated user's
   account, the most user-personal write in the codebase. Adds a
   regression test (``test_cannot_delete_me``) alongside the existing
   impersonation gate suite.

2. Gate ``GET /integrations/github_repository_benefit/user/repositories``
   with ``AuthorizeUserWrite``. The handler looks read-only at the
   route level but its service path refreshes and persists an expired
   GitHub OAuth token before making downstream API calls, so it's a
   write in disguise.

3. Migrate ``GET /stream/organizations/{id}`` to ``AuthorizeOrgAccess``
   (the ``OrgPolicyGuard`` always-allow variant). The endpoint is
   org-scoped — it takes ``{id}`` and resolves the org — so the user-
   personal ``AuthorizeOrganizationsRead`` was the wrong shelf. The
   guard now does the resolution and membership check; we drop the
   manual ``organization_service.get`` + ``ResourceNotFound`` path,
   and ``AuthorizeOrganizationsRead`` itself (no remaining users).
   Updates the handbook to reflect this and clarify that org-scoped
   reads belong with ``OrgPolicyGuard``, even when read-only.

* auth: split user-personal aliases into Web*/non-Web* prefixes

The previous commit's ``AuthorizeUser*`` aliases all routed through
``WebUserSession`` and so rejected API tokens — which broke the mobile
app's ``DELETE /v1/users/me`` flow (it authenticates with an OAuth2
access token from the PKCE flow). The single-name aliases conflated
"User subject" with "User via web session," leaving no clean way to
keep most user-personal endpoints web-only while letting a few
legitimately accept API tokens.

Split the naming so the contract is explicit:

- ``AuthorizeWeb{User,Payouts}{Read,Write}`` — User **via web session**
  only. Rejects API tokens. The right default for browser/dashboard
  flows; covers ~all migrated endpoints.
- ``Authorize{User}{Read,Write}`` — Any User subject (web, PAT, OAuth2)
  with the appropriate scope. Used only where API tokens are a valid
  caller; today that's ``DELETE /v1/users/me``.

The impersonation read-only invariant holds in both flavours:
``READ_ONLY_SCOPES`` carries no ``_write`` scope, so any
``*Write`` alias rejects impersonation regardless of prefix.

Mechanical migration: every existing ``AuthorizeUser*`` /
``AuthorizePayouts*`` annotation gets the ``Web`` prefix, and
``DELETE /v1/users/me`` gets restored to the new ``AuthorizeUserWrite``
(non-Web) variant. Tests, handbook table, and docstrings updated.

feat(receipts): add receipt download button to customer portal (#11349)

Wires the receipt download into the customer-portal order page,
gated on `order.receipt_number != null` (which is null until the
backfill runs and the per-org `receipts_enabled` flag is flipped).

Server fires `order.receipt_generated` on the customer + org SSE
channels after `receipt_path` is updated, mirroring the existing
`order.invoice_generated` publish.

The new `DownloadReceipt` component on click does an initial GET:
  - 200 (cached `receipt_path`) → opens the presigned URL
  - 202 (render enqueued) → waits for the SSE event with a 30s
    timeout, then re-fetches and opens
  - 4xx/5xx → falls into a failure UI with Try again + a plain
    `mailto:u4d33d17681682cd7@users.invalid`

The SSE listener is per-click rather than at-mount so that
background re-renders (e.g. refunds re-rendering the receipt)
don't auto-open tabs the customer didn't ask for. That's the
deliberate divergence from `DownloadInvoice`, which only fires
SSE in response to user-initiated invoice generation.

`OrderDownloadActions` orchestrates the receipt + invoice toolbar:
- Desktop: receipt button next to a kebab dropdown holding
  Download Invoice / Edit Invoice. Sized to content, right-aligned.
- Mobile: full-width stacked buttons.

Both layouts are driven by `useIsMobile`, which renders only one
`DownloadInvoicePortal` per breakpoint to avoid duplicate SSE
subscriptions on `order.invoice_generated`.

message:
ci: report skipped status when openapi check has no relevant changes (#11371)

The 'Check generated client' status is required by the main ruleset,
but the workflow used a 'paths:' filter on the trigger, so PRs that
didn't touch server/polar/** or the generated client file got no run
started — and the required check never reported, blocking merges
for unrelated PRs (e.g. handbook-only changes).

Switch to the same Detect-changes pattern used by test_server.yaml
and test_client.yaml: always run the workflow, do path filtering

* feat(organization): release slug on self-deletion

tombstone (`__deleted__-{slug}-{id}`) so the original slug is freed up

`get_user_org_ids` only filtered `UserOrganization.is_deleted`, so members of
soft-deleted organizations still received those org IDs from
`get_accessible_org_ids`. This leaked data — most notably the orders list and
CSV export — for orgs that should no longer be accessible.

Join `Organization` and filter `is_deleted`. The single caller is the
authorization helper itself, so all 40+ downstream services inherit the fix.

BLOCKED orgs are intentionally not filtered here: the codebase handles them
explicitly downstream (e.g. `Organization.can_authenticate` checks raising
`NotPermitted` → 403) so users get a clear "blocked" response rather than 404.

message:
server/refund: swallow tax transaction already reverted error (#11414)

In some complex cases with early disputes warnings and preventions, we might be in a situation where:

* A refund is created and the tax transaction is reverted to prevent a dispute
* Stripe then opens the dispute and mark it as lost (which is the expected behavior, with Verifi RDR), but also mark the refund as failed

In this case, we still need to record the dispute prevention with a proper refund, but need to account for that early refund that was marked as failed. To do so, we allow the tax transaction reversion to be skipped.

subject: fix: do not reactivate denied orgs (#11447)
message:
fix: do not reactivate denied orgs (#11447)

* fix(organization): keep admin denial sticky against post-deny webhook triggers

`maybe_activate` reverted DENIED/BLOCKED orgs to CREATED whenever
`review.is_approved` was True and onboarding wasn't ready — but
`is_approved` is True for any verdict=PASS review, including those
where an admin manually denied an AI-passed org. A subsequent Stripe
`account.updated` webhook would then flip the status back to CREATED.

Require an explicitly APPROVED appeal before re-activating from
DENIED/BLOCKED so admin denials stick.

* refactor(organization): split DENIED/BLOCKED reactivation into backoffice_approve

`maybe_activate` runs from automated triggers (Stripe webhooks, identity
verification, etc.) and previously also handled DENIED/BLOCKED orgs.
That path could quietly undo an admin's manual deny — e.g. a `pass`
verdict review left `is_approved` True, so a follow-up Stripe
`account.updated` webhook flipped DENIED back to CREATED.

Reactivating a DENIED or BLOCKED org is now a backoffice-only operation
on a dedicated `backoffice_approve` method. `maybe_activate` only
considers CREATED/REVIEW/SNOOZED. `approve_appeal` (the legitimate
DENIED → ACTIVE path) calls `backoffice_approve` directly.

* refactor(organization): restrict maybe_activate to CREATED → ACTIVE

REVIEW and SNOOZED are admin/AI review flow concerns and should not be
auto-activated by webhooks. Narrow maybe_activate accordingly.

* chore(organization): trim narration in backoffice_approve docstring and tests

* refactor(organization): make activation transitions atomic and intent-driven

Resolves a recurring bug class: a webhook calls maybe_activate on a
DENIED org and undoes the admin's manual deny because some persistent
auth signal in OrganizationReview (verdict=PASS, or appeal_decision=
APPROVED) outlives the deny.

Changes:

- maybe_activate handles only CREATED → ACTIVE. It no longer routes
  through confirm_organization_reviewed (which used to mutate
  appeal_decision as a side effect — that mutation was the recurrence
  channel).

- approve_appeal becomes synchronous: at appeal-approval time the org
  leaves DENIED *now* — to ACTIVE if onboarding gates pass, otherwise
  to CREATED. There is no "DENIED with pending reactivation" intermediate
  state for a webhook to act on.

- backoffice_approve is the explicit admin-override entry point (support
  contact, AI auto-rejected appeal, BLOCKED unblock). Synchronous,
  same-shape transition. Records the appeal as APPROVED so the merchant's
  frontend reflects the override.

- confirm_organization_reviewed now strictly handles REVIEW/SNOOZED →
  ACTIVE. The appeal-mutation hack and DENIED/BLOCKED reactivation
  branches are removed.

After this change, the org's current status is the sole source of truth
for what is authorized. A re-deny atomically puts the org back into
DENIED and webhooks cannot move it out — only an explicit human/AI
decision via approve_appeal or backoffice_approve can.

* chore(organization): lift review-threshold default to a model constant; drop :meth: markers

- Promote the hard-coded `1000` column default to
  `DEFAULT_NEXT_REVIEW_THRESHOLD_CENTS` next to the existing
  `FIRST_REVIEW_MAX_THRESHOLD_CENTS` constant.
- `_reactivate_organization` now falls back to that constant instead of
  the doubling formula. A reactivated org gets a small fresh threshold
  so the next review fires soon — the doubling pattern still applies on
  the regular REVIEW → ACTIVE path inside `confirm_organization_reviewed`.
- Strip Sphinx `:meth:` cross-reference syntax from docstrings — the
  codebase doesn't render Sphinx, so they were noise in plain reads.

* refactor(organization): unify review-threshold constants into FIRST_REVIEW_THRESHOLD_CENTS

`FIRST_REVIEW_MAX_THRESHOLD_CENTS` and the freshly-introduced
`DEFAULT_NEXT_REVIEW_THRESHOLD_CENTS` were the same value — by design,
not coincidence: an org created with the default threshold IS in its
first review cycle. Collapse them into a single constant.

subject: feat(rbac): add OrganizationRole, dual-write, validation, and backfill (#11451)
message:
feat(rbac): add OrganizationRole, dual-write, validation, and backfill (#11451)

* feat(rbac): add OrganizationRole, dual-write, validation, and backfill

Introduces the data shape for the role-based access control rollout:

- `OrganizationRole` enum (`owner`, `admin`, `member`) and a `role` column
  on `user_organizations`, NOT NULL with `server_default='member'`.
- Org creation assigns `owner` to the creator; `change_admin` swaps roles
  in the same transaction as the `Account.admin_id` mutation (previous
  owner demoted to `admin` if they currently carry it; new admin
  promoted to `owner`).
- `user_organization_service.set_role` with validation guards:
  `InvalidOwnerRoleAssignment` (only the `Account.admin_id` user may
  carry `owner`) and `OwnerRoleCannotBeRemoved` (ownership transfer
  flows through `Account.admin_id`, not the role-change path).
- `OrganizationPermission` enum, `SCOPE_IMPLIED_PERMISSIONS` mapping,
  and `ROLE_PERMISSIONS` table land in code; not consumed by any policy
  yet.
- `scripts/backfill_organization_roles.py` — idempotent, manual,
  populates `role='owner'` from `Account.admin_id`.

Authorization code still reads `Account.admin_id`; role-permission
checks ship in a follow-up.

Closes #11398
Closes #11399

* chore(rbac): rewrite backfill script to match repo convention

Use `run_batched_update` and a single batched SQL statement instead of
iterating per-org in Python. Aligns the structure with the simpler
column-update backfills (`backfill_anchor_day.py`,
`backfill_order_organization_id.py`): silent logging, locally-defined
`typer_async`, batch_size and sleep_seconds CLI options, no dry-run.

* chore(rbac): include soft-deleted rows in organization-role backfill

Drop the `deleted_at IS NULL` filters so the backfill maintains the
"Account.admin_id user carries role 'owner'" invariant on historical
data too. The dual-write paths (`change_admin`, `add_user`) don't
filter on `deleted_at` either, and `add_user` can un-delete a row
via its IntegrityError-recovery path — having the role already
correct is more robust than relying on the un-delete to also re-set
it. Composite PK on UserOrganization means at most one row per
`(user_id, organization_id)`, so the Phase 6 partial unique index
on `role = 'owner'` is unaffected.

* chore(rbac): set lock_timeout on add-role-column migration

Adds `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '2s'` so the ALTER fails fast if it
can't acquire its lock instead of queueing behind a long-running
transaction. Pattern from #11234 (psincraian's review).

* chore(rbac): apply review feedback

- Migration: switch to nullable-then-update-then-NOT-NULL pattern; the
  data backfill (everyone to 'member', then 'owner' where the user
  matches Account.admin_id) is inlined into the migration. Drops
  `server_default` so future raw SQL inserts don't silently get a
  default.
- Drop `scripts/backfill_organization_roles.py` — its work moves into
  the migration.
- Drop `server_default` on the model column; the Python-side
  `default=OrganizationRole.member` keeps ORM inserts well-formed.
- Hoist the inline `AccountRepository` import out of `set_role` to
  the module top.
- Simplify `auth/permission.py`: drop the `SCOPE_IMPLIED_PERMISSIONS`
  bridge and the `implied_permissions()` helper. Authorization is two
  consecutive gates at the policy site (existing token-scope check,
  then role-permission check); no scope-to-permission bridging table.

subject: rate-limit: short-circuit blocked callers around auth + DB (#11466)
message:
rate-limit: short-circuit blocked callers around auth + DB (#11466)

* rate-limit: cache token→identity to short-circuit before auth

Move RateLimitMiddleware ahead of AuthSubjectMiddleware/AsyncSession in
the middleware stack so a 429 short-circuits before paying for a DB
session, 5 sequential token lookups, sentry/logfire setup, and Dramatiq
enqueues.

To resolve identity without the auth stack, _authenticate parses the
bearer token from raw scope headers and looks up rl:ident:<token-hash>
in Redis (5-min TTL). On miss, it falls back to client IP.

AuthSubjectMiddleware seeds the cache after a successful non-anonymous
auth, mapping the token hash to (rate_limit_user, rate_limit_group).
This keeps RateLimitMiddleware's own counters as the single source of
truth — no separate block-state to maintain.

A single rate-limit Redis client is created at app build time, shared
between the rate-limit middleware and AuthSubjectMiddleware, and closed
in the lifespan shutdown.

* rate-limit: invalidate cache on auth failure, unify bearer parser

Address review feedback on the cached-identity approach:

- Clear rl:ident:<hash> in AuthSubjectMiddleware when auth fails for a
  bearer token. Previously a revoked token would keep counting against
  its old owner's bucket for up to 5 minutes (the cache TTL) even
  though the request itself returned 401.

- _bearer_token now decodes the Authorization header as ASCII and
  delegates to fastapi's get_authorization_scheme_param — the same
  parser get_bearer_token uses. Previously the two parsers disagreed
  on trailing whitespace, which could split per-token accounting
  between the token bucket and the IP bucket for an authenticated
  caller.

Cleanups:
- Lift _authenticate to module level; the middleware factory binds
  redis via functools.partial.
- Privatize _identity_cache_key; restore __all__ on rate_limit.
- Switch cache token type from bytes to str (parser already returns
  str).

* Include web sessions in new rate limit checks

subject: feat(authz): RBAC Phase 3 — role-permission authorization cutover (#11554)
message:
feat(authz): RBAC Phase 3 — role-permission authorization cutover (#11554)

* authz: switch policies from Account.admin_id to role-permission checks

Authorization at policy time now consults the user's `OrganizationRole`
on their membership against `ROLE_PERMISSIONS` instead of checking
`Account.admin_id` directly. The route-level token-scope check is
unchanged; the new permission check is the second gate.

- New `_require_permission` helper in `polar/authz/policies/__init__.py`
  centralises the lookup. Organization-token subjects always pass; user
  subjects are permitted iff their `UserOrganization.role` grants the
  required permission.
- `members.can_manage`, `organization.can_delete`,
  `organization.can_manage_payout_account`, `finance.can_read`,
  `finance.can_write` switched over. The old `_require_account_admin`
  helper and the inline `account_service.is_user_admin` call in the
  finance policy are gone.
- `user_organization_service.get_by_user_and_org` widened from
  `AsyncSession` to `AsyncReadSession` so the read-only policies can
  call it without a write-capable session.
- The `user_organization` test fixture now defaults to
  `role=OrganizationRole.owner` to match the post-backfill invariant
  (the fixture's `user` is `account.admin_id`); tests modeling
  non-admin scenarios downgrade explicitly.
- Policy and endpoint tests updated to set roles directly instead of
  reassigning `account.admin_id`. Error-message assertions updated
  ("Only the account admin..." → "Only an organization admin...").

* organization-member: expose role field; switch removal invariants to role

API and invariants now consult `UserOrganization.role` directly instead
of `Account.admin_id`.

- `OrganizationMember` response schema gains a `role` field; `is_admin`
  becomes a `@computed_field` derived from `role ∈ {owner, admin}`,
  with a description marking it as a transitional alias. The members
  listing endpoint drops the `OrganizationRepository.get_admin_user`
  lookup and `is_admin` post-validation patching.
- `CannotRemoveOrganizationAdmin` renamed to
  `CannotRemoveOrganizationOwner` (class + message + all importers).
  `remove_member_safe` now rejects when `user_org.role == owner`
  instead of consulting `account.admin_id`.
- `leave_organization` endpoint switched the same way: only the
  `owner` is forbidden from leaving (admins can leave if the org
  remains admin-capable).
- New `OrganizationWouldHaveNoAdmins` invariant via
  `_assert_admin_capability_after_removal` on
  `UserOrganizationService.remove_member`. Defence-in-depth: rejects
  removals that would reduce admin-capable count to zero. Non-admin
  removals from a degraded org still pass through (don't make state
  worse).
- Tests updated: exception rename + soft-delete tests use a non-admin
  member to avoid the new invariant + new tests for the
  admin-capability check.

* organization-member: ship PATCH /members/{user_id} role-change endpoint

Adds a public endpoint that lets organization admins promote a member
to admin or demote an admin back to member.

- New `members.can_set_role` policy gated by the `members:set_role`
  permission.
- New `AuthorizeMembersSetRole` dependency: route-level scope check
  for `members:write`, policy-level permission check for
  `members:set_role`.
- New `OrganizationMemberRoleUpdate` body schema with
  `role: Literal[admin, member]` — pydantic rejects `owner` at the
  schema layer (422). Ownership transfers continue to flow through
  `Account.admin_id` mutation (today: backoffice `change_admin`).
- New `PATCH /v1/organizations/{id}/members/{user_id}` endpoint
  delegates to `user_organization_service.set_role` and maps service
  exceptions to HTTP responses (404 for non-members, 403 for
  owner-demotion attempts and policy denials).
- Tests cover promote, demote, owner-in-body rejection,
  cannot-demote-owner, target-not-found, and caller-not-admin.

subject: metrics: Fix FX-incorrect credit_order contribution in fast-path revenue (#11614)
message:
metrics: Fix FX-incorrect credit_order contribution in fast-path revenue (#11614)

credit_order events don't carry their own exchange_rate, so the MV
looked one up via a self-join to the customer's most recent
balance.order. That join doesn't see prior insert batches when it
runs inside an MV trigger, and balance.order has ingestion lag while
credit_order is synchronous, so the two events basically never land
in the same batch. FX silently fell back to 1.0 and non-USD amounts
got stored as if they were USD.

Drop credit_order from the MV. Resolve it at query time in
revenue_fast instead, with the same join revenue_direct already uses
(it works fine outside an MV trigger).

Tests now ingest credit_order in a second batch so this class of bug
actually reproduces. MV needs a repopulate after deploy.

subject: authz: consolidate org/member permissions (1/5) (#11609)
message:
authz: consolidate org/member permissions (1/5) (#11609)

* authz: role-permission enforcement for admin org endpoints

Foundation refactor plus the first wave of endpoint cutover (org
settings, members, OATs, webhooks). Builds on the role/permission
model shipped in Phase 3 (#11554).

## Vocabulary

Compresses several fine-grained admin permissions into a single
`organization:manage` (covers settings update, deletion, payout
account, KYC/review, OATs, webhooks). Collapses
`members:invite`/`members:remove`/`members:set_role` into a single
`members:manage` permission alongside the existing `members:read`.
Adds `finance:read` and `finance:manage` for the finance-section
guards used by `GET /v1/organizations/{id}/account`.

## Helpers

- `assert_organization_permission(session, auth_subject, org_id, permission)`
  — service-layer mutation gate. Raises `NotPermitted` with the
  canonical message from `PERMISSION_DENIED_MESSAGE`.
- `assert_resource_permission(session, auth_subject, resource, permission)`
  — same, but reads `resource.organization_id`.
- `get_accessible_org_ids(session, auth_subject, *, permission=None)`
  — collection-read filter. Replaces the previous `_with_permission`
  variant; permission is keyword-only.
- `select_user_org_ids(user_id, *, permission=None)` — `Select` for
  use as a subquery inside `Resource.organization_id.in_(...)`.
- `PERMISSION_DENIED_MESSAGE` registry: denial messages derived from
  the permission, no `denied_msg` argument at call sites.

## Guards

- `OrgPolicyGuard(policy_fn=None, ...)` — `policy_fn` is now optional;
  `AuthorizeOrgAccess` / `AuthorizeOrgAccessUser` go through the
  membership check only. The `_always_allow` stub is gone.
- `PayoutAccountPolicyGuard()` — no `policy_fn` parameter; the
  `admin_id` ownership check is inlined.
- New `Authorize*` aliases: `AuthorizeOrgManage` (User|Org),
  `AuthorizeOrgManageUser` (User-only), `AuthorizeMembersRead`,
  `AuthorizeMembersManage`, `AuthorizeMembersSetRole`,
  `AuthorizeFinanceRead`. Old `AuthorizeOrgDelete`,
  `AuthorizeOrgManagePayoutAccount`, `AuthorizeFinanceWrite`,
  `AuthorizeOrgAccessWrite` removed.

## Endpoint cutover

`organization/endpoints.py`, `organization_access_token/{endpoints,service}.py`,
`webhook/{endpoints,service}.py`:

- Org settings update, KYC/review state, OAT CRUD, webhook CRUD +
  redeliver all gated by `organization:manage`. Members of an org
  without the admin/owner role can no longer perform these.
- `submit_review` previously used scope-only auth — closed to
  `AuthorizeOrgManage`.
- `set_payout_account` and `delete` remain User-only (destructive /
  financial-plumbing actions); other org-context endpoints accept
  org-token callers as before.

## Other changes

- Policy denial messages no longer name a role ("Only an admin
  can …" → "You don't have permission to …"). The role set can
  grow (custom roles, future ownership transfer); naming a role
  in the response is a leak.
- `polar/auth/routing.py` — `DocumentedAuthSubjectAPIRoute` now
  walks one level into a `Depends(...)` to find a nested
  `_Authenticator`, so endpoints wrapped by `OrgPolicyGuard` /
  `AccountPolicyGuard` / `PayoutAccountPolicyGuard` surface their
  required OAuth scopes in OpenAPI.
- Backoffice webhook toggle re-validates `is_blocked_webhook_host`
  (the defense the service-level URL check provides — restored after
  the service stopped being callable from the backoffice path).

## TS client

Regenerated for the new descriptions, response-model wording
changes, and the OpenAPI scope annotations that now flow through
all the policy-guard-wrapped endpoints (`Authorize*` aliases).

* authz: drop redundant `status != BLOCKED` filter

The \`Organization.status != OrganizationStatus.BLOCKED\` clauses in
\`select_user_org_ids\` and \`get_accessible_organization\` are
subsumed by \`Organization.can_authenticate\` — BLOCKED orgs have
\`api_access: False\` in their capabilities snapshot, and
\`can_authenticate\` checks exactly that (\`is_deleted = False AND
api_access = True\`).

The corresponding test was setting \`organization.status = BLOCKED\`
directly, bypassing the \`set_status()\` method that updates the
\`capabilities\` snapshot — so \`can_authenticate\` was still True
in the test even though status was BLOCKED. Use \`set_status()\` so
the test reflects how the field is actually transitioned in
production.

* backoffice/webhooks: explain why toggle bypasses the service

A reviewer flagged the backoffice toggle change as "looks unrelated".
Add a comment explaining the chain: this PR adds an
`organization:manage` assert inside `webhook_service.update_endpoint`,
the backoffice toggle has no user/org auth_subject to pass, so it
goes around the service via the repository — and the URL-block
check the service would normally apply on enable has to be
re-implemented at the call site.

subject: fix: don't double-count discounts on seat proration (#11556)
message:
fix: don't double-count discounts on seat proration (#11556)

When a subscription with a fixed-amount discount changed its seat count,
the proration logic applied the discount to the delta amount as if the
discount itself scaled with the change. For a $10 fixed discount, this
silently shaved $10 off both seat increases (under-charging) and seat
decreases (under-crediting), since the discount applies once to the
subscription total, not to every change.

Compute the discount on the old and new effective amounts instead, and
take the delta of those. Percentage discounts continue to scale linearly
and produce the same numbers; fixed discounts now cancel out in the
delta (or clamp correctly when the new base falls below the discount).

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: authz: consolidate product & custom_fields permissions (2/5) (#11610)
message:
authz: consolidate product & custom_fields permissions (2/5) (#11610)

Enforce `products:read` / `products:manage` and
`custom_fields:read` / `custom_fields:manage` across the catalog
surface, building on the helpers landed in the previous PR in the
stack.

## Wired endpoints/services

- `product/`: reads filtered by `products:read`; create / update /
  update_benefits / get_validated_prices gated by `products:manage`.
- `checkout_link/`: reads filtered by `products:read`; create / update
  / delete gated by `products:manage`.
- `discount/`: same shape — reads by `products:read`, mutations by
  `products:manage`.
- `benefit/`: same. `benefit/grant/service.list` reads filtered by
  `customers:read` (member-visible).
- `meter/`: same shape as products.
- `file/`: reads filtered by `products:read`; mutations gated by
  `products:manage` (covers `POST /files/{id}/uploaded`,
  `PATCH /files/{id}`, `DELETE /files/{id}`).
- `license_key/`: same shape. `PATCH /license-keys/{id}` mutation
  gated by `products:manage`.
- `custom_field/`: reads filtered by `custom_fields:read`; create /
  update / delete gated by `custom_fields:manage`.

## Implementation pattern

Two call-site shapes (already introduced in the previous PR):

- **Collection reads**: services call
  `get_accessible_org_ids(session, auth_subject, permission=products_read)`
  and pass the result to repository statements.
- **Resource mutations**: services / endpoints call
  `assert_resource_permission(session, auth_subject, resource, permission)`
  after fetching the resource. Callers always gate the fetch first
  (404 on missing) so the assert's 403 doesn't leak existence.

## Repository

- `discount/service._get_readable_discount_statement` and
  `custom_field/service._get_readable_custom_field_statement` use
  `select_user_org_ids(... permission=...read)` for the
  membership/role subquery (matches the pattern the previous PR
  introduced for orders/subscriptions).

## Tests

Section test suites updated for the role-permission gating; the
default `user_organization` fixture (owner role) still passes since
admin/owner carry every `*:manage` permission.

## TS client

Regenerated for the OpenAPI scope annotations that now flow through
the policy-guarded endpoints.

subject: server/order: reduce customer balance when voiding an order (#11637)
message:
server/order: reduce customer balance when voiding an order (#11637)

* server/order: reduce customer balance when voiding an order

Consider the following scenario:

* A subscription is cycled with an order of 100$. The payment is failing, and the payment is dunning.
* The customer downgrades to a 10$ plan, they get a credit of 90$ on their account.
* Later, the order is voided (either by Polar support or subscription cancellation). The customer still has a credit of 90$, even if the payment never succeeded.

This PR takes care of reducing the customer balance by the amount of the order (floored at 0) when voiding an order, so that in the scenario above, the customer would have a balance of 0$ after voiding the order.

We already had the same mechanism in place for refunds.

fix(order): prevent dunning retry for void orders (SERVER-33A) (#11680)

This fixes an inconsistent state where an Order could have status=void
but also a non-null next_payment_attempt_at field.

The issue occurred when:
- An order was voided (setting status=void and next_payment_attempt_at=None)
- The dunning task process_dunning_order was already queued for this order
- When the task executed, it would call handle_payment_failure which would
  then call _handle_first_dunning_attempt (since next_payment_attempt_at was None)
- _handle_first_dunning_attempt would set a new next_payment_attempt_at value
  without checking if the order was void

Fixes:
- Added is_void check in _handle_first_dunning_attempt to return early
- Added is_void check in process_dunning_order to skip void orders
- Added is_void.is_(False) filter in get_due_dunning_orders repository query

This also helps address Sentry issue SERVER-33A where trigger_payment
was being called for non-pending (void) orders.

message:
feat(organization_review): fetch webhook host site as a separate signal (#11686)

* feat(organization_review): fetch webhook host site as a separate signal

When an org's webhook endpoint lives on a different domain than the
declared website and the host is not on the known-integration-platform
whitelist, scrape that host's public site and feed its summary to the
review agent as a new `## Webhook Host Content` section in the prompt.

The webhook host is the merchant's stated fulfillment endpoint. When it
sits on a different domain than the declared website, that domain is
often the real product surface and the declared website may be a
placeholder. Surfacing it as a separate, labeled section lets the agent
score POLICY_COMPLIANCE and PRODUCT_LEGITIMACY on what is actually being
sold instead of on the marketing site.

Also wraps website summaries and webhook-host summaries in
`<untrusted-merchant-content>` delimiters, with a matching SYSTEM_PROMPT
section telling the agent to treat that content as data, not as
instructions. Necessary because the new collector pulls content from a
potentially adversarial host.

The webhook-host fetch chains off the setup collector inside the
existing `asyncio.gather`, so the worst-case ~90s scrape doesn't
serialize after the other collectors.

Adds 19 cloud / tunneling / automation-platform domain patterns to the
known-integration whitelist (Cloud Run, Vercel, Fly, Render, Railway,
Cloudflare Workers/Pages, AWS, Azure, ngrok, Make.com, etc.) so
legitimately cloud-hosted webhooks don't trigger the new fetch.

message:
sales: Gate order/subscription/checkout mutations on sales_manage (#11735)

Mutating endpoints on orders, subscriptions, and checkouts previously
relied solely on the scope check plus a `sales_read` readability filter
during the resource fetch. This adds an explicit `sales_manage`
permission assertion between the fetch and the mutation, matching the
refund pattern and the conventional read/manage split used elsewhere
(customers, products, analytics, finance).

Behavior no-op today — `sales_manage` is granted to all org roles and
organization-token subjects short-circuit `assert_resource_permission`.
The check is defense-in-depth if a sub-member role is ever introduced.

Covered endpoints:
- PATCH  /v1/orders/{id}
- POST   /v1/orders/{id}/invoice
- PATCH  /v1/subscriptions/{id}
- DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{id}
- POST   /v1/checkouts/
- PATCH  /v1/checkouts/{id}

Customer-portal and internal callers (dispute service, order task
flows, /v1/checkouts/client/{client_secret}) are untouched.

subject: feat: add org member role management capabilities to dashboard (#11718)
message:
feat: add org member role management capabilities to dashboard (#11718)

* authz: expose role on per-user organizations and add /roles endpoint

Two additions feeding the frontend RBAC adoption (#11402):

1. `GET /v1/organizations` for User subjects returns each org as
   `OrganizationListItem` — same as `Organization` plus a
   `role: OrganizationRole | null` field reflecting the caller's
   role on that org. Organization-token callers (org subject)
   get `null` since they represent the org itself, not a
   user-role pairing.

2. `GET /v1/organizations/{id}/roles` returns
   `[{id: <role>, permissions: [<permission strings>]}, ...]`
   derived from `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`. Static across orgs today;
   per-org route shape leaves room for org-level role
   customisation in the future.

Adds a `UserOrganizationRepository` (the module was the only one
without one) carrying a `get_roles_by_org_ids(user_id, org_ids)`
helper used by the list endpoint to bulk-fetch the caller's
per-org role.

TS client regenerated.

* dashboard: add role/permission hooks for authz cutover

Exposes the caller's role on each organization through the existing
auth context (now typed as `OrganizationListItem`) and introduces a
`useHasPermission` hook backed by a cached `/v1/organizations/{id}/roles`
query. UI code can now gate controls on the same role-permission
mapping the backend uses, without hard-coding admin checks.

* dashboard: gate members management UI by members:manage

Replaces the binary "admin / not admin" model in the Members
settings page with the RBAC role-permission system:

- Invite, role-change, and remove controls are now gated on
  `members:manage`; non-admin members see a read-only roster.
- Each row shows the member's actual role (Owner / Admin / Member)
  rather than a single "Admin" badge.
- Admins can flip other members between admin and member via an
  inline role select; the owner row is locked with a tooltip
  pointing to support, matching backend behaviour (the owner
  cannot be demoted, removed, or leave).

* dashboard: gate finance pages on finance:read permission

Income and Payouts pages previously inferred "not admin" from a
403 on the account fetch and showed an access-restricted card
worded around the legacy single-admin model. They now gate
explicitly on `finance:read`, skip the account/transaction
queries up front for users who don't have the permission, and
use copy that reflects the role-permission system instead of
naming "the admin".

* dashboard: move member row actions into a dropdown menu

Replace the inline role Select + Remove button with a single MoreVert
dropdown exposing "Change role" and "Remove from organization". Role
changes now go through a dedicated modal that defaults to the member's
current role.

* dashboard: show role permissions matrix in change role modal

Fetch organization roles via the existing /roles endpoint and render a
Permission × Role grid (Owner / Admin / Member) inside the change-role
modal, so managers can compare what each role grants before assigning.

* dashboard: scroll permissions matrix inside change role modal

Cap the matrix at 30vh with internal scrolling and a sticky header row,
so the Save and Cancel buttons stay anchored at the bottom of the modal
regardless of how many permissions a role has.

subject: Avoid overriding customer name with cardholder (#11726)
message:
Avoid overriding customer name with cardholder (#11726)

* Preserve existing customer name on checkout confirmation

When confirming a checkout with an existing customer (e.g. a company),
the cardholder name on a wallet/payment method would override
customer.name — breaking the common case where the buyer (CFO, office
manager, etc.) checks out on the customer's behalf using their personal
card.

Protect customer.name from being overridden once set; customer.billing_name
(the company name) remains updatable.

* Address review: keep Stripe customer.name in sync with Polar customer.name

- Inline the Stripe-customer name computation and drop billing_name as a
  source so Stripe's customer.name always tracks Polar's customer.name.
  billing_name remains a Polar-only concept that's freely updatable.
- Fix the comment example.
- Update the test to assert Stripe is not called with `name` when only
  billing_name changes.

* Address review: simplify name handling

- Stripe customer.name is always set from checkout.customer_billing_name
  (preferred) or checkout.customer_name on both create and update.
- Polar customer.name is only populated from the checkout for new
  customers; existing customers' names are preserved so the cardholder
  name on a wallet/payment method doesn't override them.
- Polar customer.billing_name remains freely updatable.

* Address review: rename to stripe_customer_name and clarify comment

Rename the local helper so its purpose (the name we send to Stripe) is
obvious at the call site, and rewrite the comment to spell out the
company-vs-cardholder mismatch that motivates the protection.

* Rename stripe_customer_name to customer_name

subject: feat: migrate CREATED orgs to V2 account-review onboarding (#11807)
message:
feat: migrate CREATED orgs to V2 account-review onboarding (#11807)

* scripts: enable account_review_v2 for orgs in CREATED status

Backfills feature_settings.account_review_v2_enabled = true for all
orgs currently in CREATED so they hit the new onboarding flow. New
sign-ups already get the flag at create time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* organization_review: overwrite existing review row on resubmission

The SUBMISSION agent re-run previously left non-grandfathered review
rows untouched, so a re-submit's verdict, risk score, summary, and
snapshot never reached the canonical organization_reviews row even
though status side-effects fired. The grandfathered special-case is
now the only working path. Unify both branches: any existing row is
overwritten with the latest agent run.

This makes resubmission semantics consistent and lets us safely reset
details_submitted_at for orgs stuck in CREATED so they re-enter the
new V2 onboarding flow without risking status/verdict divergence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* organization_review: clear appeal state on resubmission

Appeal fields (appeal_submitted_at, appeal_reason, appeal_reviewed_at,
appeal_decision) were tied to the previous verdict. Without clearing
them on overwrite, two failure modes appear:

- FAIL + APPROVED appeal + new DENY → row ends FAIL with appeal_decision
  still APPROVED. is_approved stays True while status flips to DENIED;
  re-appeal is locked out because appeal_decision is not None.
- FAIL + pending appeal + new PASS → review_appeal can still fire on a
  now-PASS row and run a fresh appeal review against it.

A re-submission is a fresh review event: a new FAIL gets a new appeal
opportunity, a new PASS supersedes any prior appeal. Clear all four
appeal fields on overwrite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: tighten review-overwrite and backfill-script after self-review

- Extract OrganizationReview.clear_appeal_state() for the four-field
  appeal reset, so re-submission overwrite stays a single call.
- Type _VERDICT_MAP as dict[ReviewVerdict, OrganizationReview.Verdict]
  (was `str`) and drop the redundant Verdict(mapped_verdict) wrap.
- Combine the candidate count and shape-breakdown queries in the backfill
  script — sum the per-shape n column instead of issuing a second scan.
- Drop the dated "(UI no-op today)" suffix from the shape label.
- Rename TestRunReviewAgentGrandfathered to TestRunReviewAgentSubmission;
  the class is no longer grandfathered-specific.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* review: drop docstring on clear_appeal_state

Method name speaks for itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* scripts: reset details_submitted_at for PASS+stuck CREATED orgs

Clears details_submitted_at for the cohort that already received a PASS
verdict but never reached ACTIVE — they're stuck on Stripe Identity /
Stripe Connect Express. Reset routes them to the V2 onboarding checklist
that guides them through the missing prerequisites. The existing
organization_reviews row is preserved; resubmission will trigger a
fresh agent review whose verdict overwrites it (see the SUBMISSION
re-run fix in this PR).

Filter:
  - status = 'created'
  - details_submitted_at IS NOT NULL
  - non-grandfathered PASS review
  - safety: no checkouts, no orders

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* scripts: combine v2 flag flip and details_submitted_at reset

Replace the two separate scripts with a single migrate_created_orgs_to_v2
script that runs both operations end-to-end. Drops the audit note,
50-row sample table, and shape breakdown — the dry-run just reports

* scripts: simplify reset filter to all CREATED orgs with submitted_at

    fired inline on the role transition (per the RFC).
  - `account_service.change_admin` becomes a thin orchestrator that
    delegates to `transfer_ownership` and then syncs the polar-self
    customer owner. It no longer writes `Account.admin_id`.
  - The dead `is_user_admin` helper is removed, along with two stale
    `joinedload(Account.admin)` hints whose results were never read.

The `Account.admin_id` column itself stays in place behind this commit
so old rows aren't stranded; the column drop ships next.

Refs #11404

* rbac: drop Account.admin_id column and dual-write

Now that nothing reads `Account.admin_id` (previous commit), retire the
column and the helpers that fed it:

  - Destructive migration drops `accounts.admin_id`. Downgrade reinstates
    it nullable and backfills from the user holding `owner` on each
    organization, restoring the previous invariant for rollback.
  - `Account.admin_id` mapped column and `Account.admin` relationship
    removed from the model.
  - `account_service.create` no longer takes the founding admin user;
    the caller in `organization_service.create` is the only site.
  - Test fixtures (`create_account`, `generate_account`) no longer set
    `admin_id` on the constructed `Account`.

Closes #11404

* rbac: rename admin→owner across the org-ownership surface

Now that `Account.admin_id` is gone, "admin" is an overloaded word: the
backoffice still uses it for Polar staff, `UserOrganization.role` still
has an `admin` role distinct from `owner`, and `PayoutAccount.admin_id`
is its own thing. Anywhere the codebase said "admin" but meant "the
user who owns the organization", rename to `owner`:

  - `OrganizationRepository.get_admin_user` → `get_owner_user`
  - `account_service.change_admin` → `change_owner`
    (params `new_admin_id`/`new_admin_user` → `new_owner_id`/`new_owner_user`)
  - `CannotChangeAdminError` → `CannotChangeOwnerError`
  - Backoffice route `/make-admin/` (`organizations:make_admin`,
    `make_admin`) → `/make-owner/` (`organizations:make_owner`,
    `make_owner`); UI labels follow ("Make Owner", "Owner",
    "Ownership Transfer Requirements", "New owner must be verified",
    "Transfer ownership to this user?", "No owner user found").
  - Local variables across `organization/service.py`,
    `organization_review/agent.py`, the backoffice endpoints/views, and
    `scripts/plain_comm.py`: `admin_user`/`admin_user_id`/`admin_email`
    → `owner_user`/`owner_user_id`/`owner_email`; backoffice team
    rendering's `is_admin`/`member_is_admin` → `is_owner`/`member_is_owner`.
  - `TestChangeAdminRoleSwap` → `TestChangeOwnerRoleSwap`; test method
    names follow.

Also fix the backoffice manual-payout-account endpoint to set the org
owner as the new `PayoutAccount.admin`, replacing the previous
arbitrary `users[0]` pick. The owner is the user who's already been
identity-verified for payouts and is the natural party responsible for
the payout account.

Deliberately left alone: `User.is_admin` (platform/staff flag),
`PayoutAccount.admin_id` (separate ownership concept), and the
`admin_user_id`/`admin_email` log fields that name the backoffice
staff operator rather than the org owner.

Refs #11404

* rbac: review-feedback cleanups

- Partial unique index migration now uses `op.create_index(op.f(...))`
  with `postgresql_concurrently=True` inside an autocommit block,
  matching the neighbouring 2026-05-20-0853 migration. Avoids a SHARE
  lock on `user_organizations` during deploy.
- `transfer_ownership`: drop the redundant `UserRepository.get_by_id`
  lookup — the user is now loaded via the joined `user_org.user`
  relationship that `get_by_user_and_org` already eager-loads. One
  round-trip saved and the misleading "user doesn't exist →
  UserNotMemberOfOrganization" error path is gone. Wrap the promote
  UPDATE in try/except IntegrityError that translates to AlreadyOwner
  when a concurrent transfer wins the race against the partial unique
  index, so callers see a clean application error instead of a raw
  DB exception.
- `change_owner`: drop the unused `account: Account` parameter and the
  pass-through return value; convert remaining args to keyword-only.
  Caller in the backoffice endpoint loses the now-unneeded
  `joinedload(Organization.account)` accordingly.
- Update the stale fixture comment that referenced `account.admin_id`.

Refs #11404

* backoffice: refresh ownership transfer requirements card

The card listed three rules but only one ("new owner must be verified")
was actually enforced by `transfer_ownership`. Replace with the three
real preconditions / consequences:

  - new owner must already be a member of the organization
  - new owner must have completed Stripe identity verification
  - current owner is demoted to admin (they keep access)

Drop the stale "no Stripe account connected" and "≥2 team members"
items — neither is enforced anywhere in code.

`transfer_ownership` rejects unverified users with `NewOwnerNotVerified`,

(which didn't declare it). Add it to `__table_args__` so the model is

Both files were hand-authored; rewrite them starting from what `alembic

* fix(rate-limit): isolate pending_auth requests to per-endpoint zones

Requests with an unvalidated bearer token / cookie are classified as
RateLimitGroup.pending_auth. _BASE_RULES only defined default-group rules
for sensitive endpoints, so pending_auth requests fell through to the
catch-all "^/v1" rule with zone="api" — bypassing the strict
endpoint-specific zones (login-code, customer-session-login,
checkout-confirm, etc.) and their block_time settings.

Add a pending_auth twin Rule to every entry in _BASE_RULES with the same
zone, limits, and block_time. Adds parametrized regression coverage that
walks rule selection the same way ratelimit/core.py does, asserting both
default and pending_auth groups resolve to the endpoint's dedicated zone
for all 7 sensitive paths in both production and sandbox rule sets.

message:
fix(benefit): stop resetting meters when refreshing benefit grants (#11853)

* fix(benefit): stop resetting meters when refreshing benefit grants (#11427)

The benefit grant pipeline was unconditionally calling
`subscription_service.reset_meters`, which emits a `meter_reset` event
scoped to (customer, meter) globally. That wiped credits from unrelated
active subscriptions whenever a merchant edited a product's benefits.

Meter resets are now solely the responsibility of
`order.service.create_subscription_order` (for cycle/cancel orders) and
`meter_credit.cycle()` per grant. This also aligns with the explicit
"subscription_update is intentionally excluded" intent already documented
in the order layer.

Revoke + grant is symmetric (meter_credit.revoke emits the matching
negative-units event), so balances still settle correctly on product
change without a reset in between.

* test(meter_credit): lock in usage-carryover semantics on upgrade

Adds a regression test that fails if a meter_reset is reintroduced on
the subscription-update path. Verifies the design established by
6e1d2513e: when a customer upgrades mid-cycle, prior usage persists and
counts against the new plan's credit allowance (balance = 920, not
1000).

This complements the existing test_upgrade_balance_without_meter_reset,
which only covered the no-usage case where reset vs. no-reset both land
at 1000.

* refactor(benefit): rename actor to benefit.enqueue_grants

The benefit.reset_meters_and_enqueue_grants actor no longer resets
meters; the name was kept only to drain in-flight Dramatiq messages
during the rollout. Register the new name now and keep the old one as
a thin alias so the rename is locked in immediately and there's no
follow-up rename to remember. The alias can be deleted once the queue
has drained after deploy.

`benefit_enqueue_grants(...)`, which routes through the actor

subject: fix: preserve scheduled product changes when seats change (#11129) (#11831)
message:
fix: preserve scheduled product changes when seats change (#11129) (#11831)

Scheduled subscription product changes with proration_behavior=next_period
were silently dropped when seats were modified before the boundary.

Two write paths needed fixing:

- SubscriptionUpdateRepository.upsert overwrote every column on the
  pending row unconditionally, blanking the other dimension. Merge fields
  conditionally instead, checking object.product (not product_id) because
  SQLAlchemy doesn't sync the FK on a transient instance until flush.

- SubscriptionService.update_seats immediate-proration branch soft-deleted

subject: Skip invoice regeneration when inputs are unchanged (#11900)
message:
Skip invoice regeneration when inputs are unchanged (#11900)

* Skip invoice regeneration when inputs are unchanged

POST /v1/orders/{id}/invoice currently always enqueues a regeneration
task, even when the inputs that affect the rendered PDF haven't changed.
This wastes worker capacity and S3 bandwidth on no-op renders.

Adds an `orders.invoice_checksum` column that captures the rendered
state. The trigger short-circuits when the stored checksum matches a
freshly-computed one (NULL checksums on legacy rows fall through and
regenerate as before — no backfill needed).

Checksum is SHA-256 over a JSON-encoded payload of
`INVOICE_TEMPLATE_VERSION`, `billing_name`, `billing_address`,
`tax_id`, and `customer.locale`. Bump `INVOICE_TEMPLATE_VERSION` when
the template or seller-side settings change.

* Drop autogenerate comment markers from migration

* Log when invoice generation is scheduled vs skipped

* Use dot-namespaced event names for invoice generation logs

* Short-circuit invoice generation in the worker too

Makes the worker idempotent so already-queued jobs become no-ops when
the order's checksum already matches its on-disk invoice. Removes the
need for a queue-cancellation script: pending jobs simply skip if
nothing has changed by the time they run.

* Stub invoice_service.compute_order_checksum in e2e mock

* Re-point invoice_checksum migration onto latest main head

* Address PR review: drop redundant assert, use pytest fixture

The Stripe webhook handler upserts the failed Payment row before

subject: fix: raise on agent review failure instead of persisting synthetic DENY (#11904)
message:
fix: raise on agent review failure instead of persisting synthetic DENY (#11904)

When the Pydantic AI gateway returns a transient error (429, 5xx,
connection failure), the analyzer used to swallow the exception and
return a fake DENY report. That row was then committed as a real
verdict, auto-denying merchant submissions and auto-rejecting their
appeals during upstream outages.

The analyzer now re-raises every non-success path. Dramatiq retries the
actor (max_retries=4, min_backoff=30s) so brief blips self-heal, and on
exhaustion Sentry captures the failure for engineer alerting. The org
stays in its current status rather than transitioning to denied, so
real bugs and outages surface as engineer signals instead of misleading
merchant denials.

Same policy now applies to threshold reviews: a failed threshold check
retries and alerts rather than silently dropping the verdict.

subject: fix: partial unique index on organization_reviews (#11944)
message:
fix: partial unique index on organization_reviews (#11944)

The unique index on `organization_reviews(organization_id)` did not
filter on `deleted_at`, so a soft-deleted row blocked any subsequent
INSERT for the same organization. The SUBMISSION review worker then
crashed with `UniqueViolationError` and DLQed; affected dashboards
polled `/review-status` indefinitely showing "Reviewing organization…"
with no verdict and no recovery path.

Swap the index for a partial one (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`) — the
established Polar pattern for soft-deletable models with per-parent
uniqueness (see e.g. `discount_ignore_soft_deletes`,
`add_partial_unique_owner_index`, the `members`, `subscription_update`,
`user_organization`, `discount` models, etc.).

With this index, soft-deleted rows coexist with new live rows: the
existing SUBMISSION worker's lookup → INSERT path now succeeds on
resubmission after a cleanup. No worker change required.

subject: fix: collapse duplicate org review runs and make confirm atomic (#11943)
message:
fix: collapse duplicate org review runs and make confirm atomic (#11943)

* fix: collapse duplicate org review runs and make confirm atomic

A single order writes several balance rows (charge + platform fee +
reversal fees), and each row enqueues `organization.check_threshold`.
On threshold-crossing orders the resulting concurrent tasks all flipped
ACTIVE→REVIEW and each spawned its own agent run.

The post-verdict doubling in `confirm_organization_reviewed` then read
the in-memory snapshot, so N parallel verdicts after a long LLM call
all doubled from the same starting value — collapsing into a single
effective doubling and leaving the org's next-review threshold stuck.

Two changes:

- `organization.check_threshold` actor gets `debounce_key=…` keyed on
  account_id (same pattern as `customer_meter.update_customer`), so
  bursts from one business event collapse to a single execution.
- `confirm_organization_reviewed` is rewritten as an atomic
  `UPDATE … WHERE status IN (REVIEW, SNOOZED) RETURNING` with
  server-side doubling via `func.greatest(threshold * 2, min)`.
  Returns `Organization | None`; `None` = another worker won the race.

`handle_ongoing_review_verdict` now reports True/False based on whether
THIS worker won, so only the winner records the agent decision.

Added two race-safety tests:
- race-loss → None
- doubling reads the DB row, not a stale snapshot

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* address review: 409 status + RETURNING

- confirm_organization_reviewed now raises OrganizationError(409) with
  the org id in the message, matching state-conflict semantics elsewhere
  in the codebase (exceptions.py:130, auth/endpoints.py:212).
- confirm_review_atomic now returns Organization | None via
  UPDATE ... RETURNING + populate_existing=True (the kit/services.py
  idiom). Drops the redundant session.refresh round-trip and the cast
  to CursorResult — the typed scalar_one_or_none result is enough.

subject: fix: set correct status_code on redirect exceptions to suppress Sentry noise (#11984)
message:
fix: set correct status_code on redirect exceptions to suppress Sentry noise (#11984)

* Fix exception status codes to prevent spurious Sentry reports

Sentry's StarletteIntegration wraps every registered exception handler
with `_sentry_patched_exception_handler`, which checks
`hasattr(exp, "status_code") and exp.status_code in
failed_request_status_codes` (default: 5xx) BEFORE delegating to the
real handler. The HTTP response status is irrelevant — only the
exception object's status_code attribute matters at capture time.

Several Polar exceptions inherited PolarError's default status_code=500
despite having handlers that returned redirect responses. This caused
Sentry to report exceptions that were intentionally handled.

- PolarAuthRedirectionError: now sets status_code=302; handler uses
  exc.status_code instead of hardcoded 303.
- PolarRedirectionError: default status_code changed from 400 to 303
  (matching what the handler returns); handler uses exc.status_code.
- Drop the meaningless `e.status_code` argument from callers that were
  forwarding upstream HTTP status codes into the redirect (which would
  otherwise produce non-3xx redirects and reintroduce 5xx status codes
  on the exception instance).

Co-Authored-By: u70c8551349ddf3cb <u70c8551349ddf3cb@users.invalid>

* Match PolarAuthRedirectionError status_code to handler's 303 redirect

The auth_redirection_error_exception_handler returns a 303 redirect via
RedirectResponse(error_url, exc.status_code), so the exception's
status_code should be 303 (not 302) to preserve the original handler
behavior.

Co-Authored-By: u70c8551349ddf3cb <u70c8551349ddf3cb@users.invalid>

subject: server/auth: don't pre-create user when requesting email OTP (#12045)
message:
server/auth: don't pre-create user when requesting email OTP (#12045)

* Revert "server/auth: create user if does not exist when requesting email OTP (#12044)"

This reverts commit a26edf84a9ffe5f688641512ace24d56db60bbf1.

* server/auth: don't pre-create user when requesting email OTP

In a26edf84a9ffe5f688641512ace24d56db60bbf1, we made an emergency fix to allow new users to sign up with email OTP. Indeed, the `request` method was silently no-op if  the user was not already existing. This quick fix made sure to pre-create the user before proceeding.

However, this wasn't the intended implementation. In `/email-otp/verify` endpoint, we had dedicated logic to create the user after a successful OTP verification. This means that the user should only be created after the OTP is verified, and not before.

The current fix is the right one: we send the email in all cases, even if the user is not yet created. The user will only be created after the OTP is verified, which is the expected flow.

subject: Handle rate-limit responses gracefully in auth middleware (#12042)
message:
Handle rate-limit responses gracefully in auth middleware (#12042)

* fix(web): handle 429 from /v1/users/me in proxy instead of 500ing

The Next.js proxy middleware fetches /v1/users/me (cache: no-cache) on
every navigation that carries the session cookie. When that request is
rate-limited upstream — the cookie gets counted in the API's
`pending_auth` bucket (10/min, the lowest limit in the system) — the
middleware only tolerated 401 and threw on any other non-OK status,
turning a transient 429 into a hard 500 ("Unexpected response status
while fetching authenticated user").

Treat 429 as "couldn't determine the user" and proceed as anonymous
(protected routes redirect to login, mirroring the existing 401 path),
while still logging it so we keep visibility on how often it happens.
Genuinely unexpected statuses (e.g. 5xx) keep failing loudly.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01D8MApm2fQyBwE92vEHrCpG

* fix(api): raise pending_auth rate limit from 10 to 60/min

/v1/users/me is fetched by the web proxy on every navigation that
carries the session cookie, and lands in the `pending_auth` bucket
whenever the identity cache is cold or the cookie is expired/invalid.
At 10/min a single page's cold-cache fan-out (middleware + SSR fetches
+ link prefetch) could exceed it, producing 429s for legitimate
traffic.

The bucket is keyed per-credential-value (token:/cookie: hash), so this
limit only governs how fast a single unvalidated credential can hit the
API before it's promoted to its real group. It does not bound credential
guessing across many distinct values (that's handled per-endpoint with
block_time on the sensitive auth routes), so raising it is safe and
gives cold-cache / expired-cookie traffic enough headroom. Applied to
both production and sandbox.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01D8MApm2fQyBwE92vEHrCpG

* fix(web): treat 429 from /v1/auth/status as no session, not a 500

When the proxy gets a 429 on /v1/users/me it now redirects to /auth.
But /auth's server component calls checkAuthenticationSession ->
GET /v1/auth/status, which sits in the same per-cookie `pending_auth`
bucket and will also 429 in the same burst. That path threw, so a
rate-limited user simply had their 500 moved from /dashboard to /auth.

Treat a 429 as "no active session" (return null) so /auth degrades to
the login form instead of crashing; the user recovers on the next
navigation once the identity cache warms. Unexpected non-OK responses
(e.g. 5xx) still throw. This fulfills #12036's stated intent of handling
the 429 gracefully (the throw it shipped was not graceful).
