subject: ci(deploy): diff against last-deployed SHA via git tags (#11961)
message:
ci(deploy): diff against last-deployed SHA via git tags (#11961)

* ci(deploy): diff against last-deployed SHA via git tags

Fixes a silent-skip bug in the deploy workflow: when concurrency cancels
a pending run (a third push arrives while one is in progress and another
is pending), the next run's `paths-filter` only diffs against the
immediate parent (`github.event.before`) — so any backend or frontend
changes in the cancelled middle commit are never detected and never
deployed.

Real incident: PR #11943 (a backend-only fix) was sandwiched between
backend and frontend merges, its run got cancelled, and its backend
changes were not deployed by any subsequent run.

Fix: replace the implicit "diff against parent" base with an explicit
"diff against the last successfully deployed SHA for this component +
environment". Four tags track state:

  deployed/backend-sandbox
  deployed/backend-production
  deployed/frontend-sandbox
  deployed/frontend-production

After each successful component deploy, the corresponding tag advances
to the deployed SHA. The next run's `changes` job uses that tag as the
diff base. Cancelled intermediate runs are now harmless: the next run
still sees the dropped commits because the tag hasn't moved.

Per-component, per-environment because:
  - sandbox can be ahead of production (failed prod deploy leaves
    sandbox tag advanced)
  - frontend-only push must not advance backend tag, else a later
    cancelled backend run would lose its commits

Tag-update jobs are split per component, each gated only on its own
deploy's success. A frontend failure does not pin the backend tag at a
stale SHA, so we avoid redundant Render redeploys on the next push.

Bootstrap: before merging this PR, create the four tags pointing at
current `main` HEAD (see PR description for the one-liner). On the first
deploy after merge, the workflow falls back to `github.event.before` if
a tag is missing — so a missing-tag situation is degraded behavior, not
broken.

Bonus DX win: any engineer can run
  git log deployed/backend-production..main -- server/
locally to see exactly what's pending deploy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(deploy): fix code-review findings on tag-based deploy filter

Seven defects surfaced during xhigh-effort review of 166b8982e:

1. **Frontend filter used the BACKEND tag as base** (critical, the bug
   the PR claimed to fix, mirrored to frontend). `dorny/paths-filter@v4`
   uses a single base across all filters in one invocation. With only
   two invocations (one per env) both filters shared the backend tag,
   so a frontend deploy that failed after a backend success would have
   its pending frontend changes permanently lost from future diffs.
   Fixed by splitting into four paths-filter invocations: one per
   component per environment, each with its own correct base.

2. **Sandbox tag-push failure blocked production deploy.** The
   workflow_call's overall result was failure if any update-*-tag job
   failed, which gated deploy-production via `!failure()`. A transient
   git push hiccup would turn into a hard production-deploy outage.
   Fixed by adding `continue-on-error: true` to all tag-update jobs:
   the worst case is now a redundant redeploy on the next push (safe,
   idempotent), never a production outage.

3. **Missing top-level `permissions:` block in deploy.yml.** Reusable
   workflows' per-job permissions are capped by the caller's effective
   token scope. If the repo's default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only, the
   per-job `contents: write` declarations in the tag-update jobs would
   return 403. Fixed by declaring `permissions: contents: write,
   packages: write` at the top of deploy.yml.

4. **`github.event.before` empty on workflow_dispatch** (and zero-SHA
   on first push to a branch) flowed through the fallback into
   paths-filter as `base: ''`, with undefined behavior — potentially
   blocking the entire pipeline on operator-triggered redeploys. Fixed
   by detecting empty / zero-SHA / non-resolvable event.before and
   falling back to HEAD~1 (always available with fetch-depth: 0).

5. **`set -e` did NOT propagate failures from `$(resolve ...)` inside
   command substitution.** A transient git failure inside the resolve
   helper would silently emit `key=` (empty value) instead of aborting
   the step. Fixed by `shopt -s inherit_errexit` after `set -euo
   pipefail` in all run: blocks that use command substitution.

6. **Sentry release failure marked deploy-backend as failed** even
   when Render was already live. Combined with #4, this would turn a
   rotated SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN into a production-deploy outage. Fixed by
   moving Sentry release into its own job (`sentry-release`) with
   `continue-on-error: true`: Sentry annotations are best-effort
   observability, not a deploy gate.

7. **`git push -f` without `--force-with-lease`** could blindly stomp
   a concurrent tag advance from a hotfix automation or operator. Also
   added re-fetch between retries so the lease check sees the current
   remote state. Mitigated today by the workflow-level concurrency
   group but no longer brittle to future parallelism changes.

Also adds `--prune --prune-tags` to the initial fetch, defensive against
self-hosted/cached runners (currently a no-op on ephemeral Blacksmith
runners but cheap insurance).

Not fixed (acceptable risk, documented as comments where useful):
- Tag pointing to unreachable SHA after force-push to main (rare;
  manual recovery is trivial)
- Operator re-running an old failed workflow advances tag to old SHA
  (operator footgun; would require deeper redesign to prevent)
- Cached-runner stale-tag concern (we use ephemeral runners)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(deploy): harden + simplify tag-based deploy filter (review round 2)

Applies the must-fix and should-fix findings from the second review pass,
keeping the 4-tag approach but removing the sharpest edges.

- **F1 (must-fix):** the changes-job `git fetch --tags ...` ran bare under
  `set -euo pipefail`. A transient fetch failure would abort the changes
  job and block ALL deploys. Made non-fatal with `|| true` — checkout
  (fetch-depth: 0) already fetches all tags, so this fetch is purely
  defensive.

- **F2:** workflow_dispatch can run from any ref. The tag-push jobs would
  push deployed/* to that ref's SHA, poisoning the diff base for every
  later main push (silent skips). Guarded both tag jobs with
  `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`.

- **F4:** the standalone sentry-release job declared `environment:`. If the
  GitHub Environment has required reviewers / a wait timer, that job would
  pause for approval, stalling deploy-sandbox and blocking deploy-production.
  Dropped the job-level `environment:` (the Sentry-side label uses the
  action's own input, so release tracking is unchanged).

- **F6 + F8 (simplification):** replaced the force-with-lease + REMOTE_SHA +
  per-iteration-fetch dance with a plain `git push -f`. The lease gave only
  illusory protection here (the retry re-fetch re-armed it to a competitor's
  SHA anyway), and the plain-push fallback was guaranteed-rejected for an
  existing tag on a persistent fetch failure. Plain force is safe because
  the top-level `build-deploy` concurrency group serializes deploy runs
  (no overlapping tag-push windows) and the jobs are now main-guarded. This
  also drops the now-unneeded `fetch-tags` and `shopt inherit_errexit` from
  the tag jobs and fixes the stale "depth >= 2" comment.

- **F9 (security/least-privilege):** the changes job inherited workflow-level
  `contents: write` but only reads. Pinned it to `contents: read` so a
  compromised pinned action there can't push to the repo or to deployed/*.

Still recommended before/at merge (not code, noted in PR):
- Verify the sandbox/production GitHub Environments have no required-reviewer
  gates (otherwise deploy-backend/promote-frontend already gate — unrelated
  to this PR but worth confirming).
- Empirically confirm continue-on-error on the tag jobs leaves the reusable
  workflow's conclusion = success (force one tag-push failure on sandbox and
  check deploy-production still launches).
- Bootstrap the four deployed/* tags at the ACTUAL currently-deployed prod
  SHA before the first run; a too-new bootstrap silently drops pending commits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(deploy): close empty-digest gap + harden args (review round 3)

Third review pass. Prior rounds caught the structural issues; this pass
found one real (narrow) bug plus two hardening items.

- **deploy-sandbox empty-digest on dispatch (CONFIRMED bug):** the
  deploy-sandbox gate lacked `!failure()` (deploy-production already had
  it). If the `changes` job fails, `build` is skipped (it has no
  `if: always()`), and on a workflow_dispatch the `|| workflow_dispatch`
  clause would still let deploy-sandbox run with an empty
  `needs.build.outputs.digest`, deploying `ghcr.io/polarsource/polar@`
  (malformed) to sandbox. Added `!failure() && !cancelled()` to mirror
  deploy-production. Normal frontend-only pushes (build skipped, changes
  succeeded) are unaffected — skipped is not failure.

- **Unquoted deploy_server.sh args (defense-in-depth):** quoted
  `inputs.docker-digest` and `inputs.has-migrations` in the script call.
  Unquoted, an empty digest would vanish and shift every positional arg
  left (service IDs mapping to the wrong parameters) while still passing
  the script's `[ $# -lt 4 ]` guard. Quoting keeps the arg positions
  stable. (The reachable empty-digest path is closed by the fix above;
  this is belt-and-suspenders.)

- **Redundant fetch-tags (cleanup):** dropped `fetch-tags: true` from the
  changes-job checkout — `fetch-depth: 0` already fetches all tags.

Reviewed but deliberately NOT changed (pre-existing / behavior decisions,
noted for follow-up):
- workflow_dispatch from a non-main branch still deploys that branch to
  production (the round-2 ref-guard only protects the tag push). Guarding
  the deploy jobs to main is a behavior decision, left to maintainers.
- A sandbox-side failure blocks the unrelated production deploy via the
  `!failure()` gate, and within an env a backend failure blocks frontend
  promotion. Pre-existing job-graph coupling; decoupling is a larger
  restructure.
- migration ordering only keys off `server/migrations/**` (same detection
  scope as the original workflow).
- continue-on-error not propagating through the reusable-workflow
  conclusion is documented-correct but worth a one-time empirical check.
- tag-push bash / paths-filter duplication left as-is: YAML anchors and a
  composite action add parse-time/indirection risk to a deploy-critical,
  untestable-before-merge file for modest gain.

subject: fix: bill first graduated seat tier from seat 1 (#12075)
message:
fix: bill first graduated seat tier from seat 1 (#12075)

Graduated seat pricing sized each tier's capacity from its own min_seats.
The first tier's min_seats doubles as the minimum order quantity, so when
a merchant set it above 1 to enforce a minimum, the first tier's capacity
collapsed and the lower seats spilled into cheaper tiers, undercharging.

Measure each tier's capacity from the previous tier's upper bound (0 for
the first tier) so the first tier always bills from seat 1. Behavior is
identical for all configs whose first tier starts at 1.

subject: Off-session draft-order charges (#12089)
message:
Off-session draft-order charges (#12089)

* orders: off-session draft-order charges

Adds the off-session charge API: draft orders (nullable invoice_number),
the off_session_charges_enabled organization flag, create / finalize
endpoints and service with an OrderPolicyGuard, plus client SDK, mobile
app, and backoffice surfacing. Off-session charges are rejected for
seat-based products.

* product: enforce currency minimum for all positive custom amounts

validate_custom_price_amount only checked the processor floor when the
configured minimum was 0. Enforce it for any positive amount (mirroring
the currency-maximum check) so an amount below the currency minimum can't
pass validation and then fail at charge time.

Addresses CodeRabbit review on #12089.

* orders: address CodeRabbit review on off-session charges

- reject draft creation when tax can't be computed (e.g. the customer's
  billing address is missing/invalid) instead of persisting a tax-free
  draft that finalize never recomputes; subscription flow keeps its
  tolerant warn-and-zero behavior via allow_silent_failure
- allocate the invoice number before emitting paid hooks on the
  under-currency-minimum settle path, so order.paid webhooks never observe
  invoice_number=None (idempotent; no-op for orders that already have one)
- include the organization id in OffSessionChargesNotEnabled /
  OrganizationNotReadyForPayments messages
- tests: lost draft-claim guard, uncomputable-tax rejection, and finalize
  402/403 endpoint mappings

* orders: restrict off-session charges to fixed-price products

Off-session draft orders now only accept one-time, fixed-price products;
pay-what-you-want (custom) and free products are rejected. The amount is
fully determined by the product, so the OrderCreate.amount field is
removed. (Support for merchant-set amounts arrives with the set-on-order
price type in the follow-up PR.)

* orders: address review — optional currency + dedicated custom_price module

- POST /v1/orders accepts an optional `currency` so the merchant can force
  a specific currency; required only when the product is priced in more
  than one currency, otherwise the single currency is used
- move validate_custom_price_amount out of price_set.py into a dedicated
  polar/product/custom_price.py module (per review)

* orders: fall back to org default currency for off-session charges

Match the checkout flow: when no currency is given, resolve the
off-session draft order against the organization's default presentment
currency instead of rejecting multi-currency products. A currency only
needs to be passed when the product isn't priced in the org default.

* product: narrow validate_custom_price_amount to CustomPrice

Accept a CustomPrice rather than a base ProductPrice so minimum_amount /
maximum_amount are statically typed as int (never None), addressing the
nullable-minimum concern via the type system instead of a runtime guard.
All call sites already narrow with is_custom_price first, so the internal
no-op guard is redundant and removed.

* orders: assert selected price set in multi-currency draft-order tests

Assert the resolved items/subtotal, not just order.currency, so the tests
catch a resolver that stamps the right currency but picks the wrong price
set (usd 1000 vs eur 900 vs gbp 800).

subject: feat: allow held payouts for organizations under review (#12097)
message:
feat: allow held payouts for organizations under review (#12097)

* feat: allow held payouts for organizations under review

Phase 2 of the payout-reviews RFC. Organizations in REVIEW or SNOOZED can
now request a payout; it is created as `held` (balance reserved, Stripe
transfer skipped) and released to `pending` when the org is approved, or
canceled with a full refund (gross plus fees) when the org is denied,
blocked, offboarded, or swaps its payout account.

- Flip the `payouts` capability to true for REVIEW/SNOOZED, with a backfill
  script for orgs already under review.
- Branch PayoutService.create on org status under a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
  lock; rename OrganizationUnderReview -> OrganizationCannotPayout.
- Split payout.created into an event task plus a new payout.transfer task;
  lock + re-read in transfer_stripe so it never moves funds for a
  canceled/held payout.
- Reverse per-payout fees on cancel; lock + re-check in cancel to prevent
  concurrent double-credits.
- Wire release/cancel jobs into the org lifecycle transitions.
- Repository fixes: get_all_stripe_pending filters to pending; held payouts
  count against payout accounts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: trim payout-review comments to non-obvious notes

Cut narration that restated self-explanatory code; kept concise "why" notes
for the concurrency locks, ledger/fee-reversal reasoning, and the capability
semantic change. Also dropped em dashes from the new backfill script copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: skip admin-disabled payouts in the capability backfill

The backfill flips payouts to true for REVIEW/SNOOZED orgs whose stored
capability is false, but an admin may have deliberately disabled payouts on a
specific org. Exclude orgs carrying the set_capability disable marker in their
internal notes so the backfill never re-enables an intentional block. No-op at
the initial deploy (disabling an already-false default left no note); protects
re-runs once payouts defaults to true.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: emit an event for held-payout cancel on payout-account swap

set_payout_account used a function-local import of payout.service to cancel
held payouts on a Connect-account swap, pulling the payout layer into the
organization service to dodge a circular import. Replace it with an
`organization.cancel_held_payouts` event (enqueue_job is string-dispatched, no
import) handled in organization.tasks, which already owns the payout-service
dependency. Behaviour is unchanged (held-only cancel); it's just async now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: move held-payout jobs to the payout module

The release/cancel jobs operate on payouts, not organizations, so move them
out of organization.tasks (under organization.* actor names) into payout.tasks
as payout.release_held_payouts / payout.cancel_account_payouts /
payout.cancel_held_payouts. The organization service still drives them via
enqueue_job (string dispatch), so it gains no payout import; organization.tasks
drops its payout.service / PayoutStatus imports entirely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: drop redundant count logs from release/cancel payout jobs

The job queue already records the enqueued payout.transfer messages and the
worker logs each actor run, so the per-call "released/canceled N" info logs
were duplicate observability. Removed them (and the now-unused counter).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: drop internal-note override check from the capability backfill

The backfill runs once at deploy. Before the flip, REVIEW/SNOOZED already
defaulted to payouts=false and set_capability no-ops on a same-value write, so
no deliberate "payouts disabled" override (or its note) can exist yet. The
note-based skip therefore matched nothing on the real run — pure complexity.
Reverts to a plain capability check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Scope held-payout cancel and guard transfer against payout-account swaps

Addresses two race conditions around held payouts and Connect-account swaps:

- set_payout_account now passes the previous payout_account_id to
  payout.cancel_held_payouts, so the swap-cancel only touches holds pinned to
  the stale account and can't sweep up a fresh hold created against the new
  account once the 24h cooldown clears.

- transfer_stripe re-checks, before moving any funds, that the payout's pinned
  payout_account still matches the org's current one. If the org swapped after
  the hold was released (release can win the race against the swap-cancel job),
  it cancels and refunds instead of transferring to the abandoned account.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move transfer guards to processor-agnostic transfer + lock to the task

Addresses maintainer review on the held-payout swap fixes:

- Extract a processor-agnostic PayoutService.transfer that re-checks the payout
  is payable and guards against a payout-account swap, then dispatches to the
  processor. transfer_stripe is now a pure Stripe primitive (no lock, no
  guards), so a future non-Stripe processor inherits the guards.
- Acquire the FOR UPDATE lock in the payout.transfer task (its sole caller)
  rather than inside the service, keeping transfer pure decision logic.
- Rename "Connect" to "payout account" in processor-agnostic comments; leave
  genuinely Stripe-specific docstrings untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Lock the payout row via get_by_id_for_update in the transfer task

Replace the load + session.refresh(with_for_update) two-step with a single
PayoutRepository.get_by_id_for_update that selects the payout under FOR UPDATE
OF payouts, matching the get_by_id_for_update convention used elsewhere
(checkout, discount). The OF clause locks only the payout row so eager-load
joins don't trip the nullable-outer-join lock error. Adds a repository test
exercising the locked eager query against Postgres.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The off-session amount validation only checked the currency minimum, so a
custom amount above the currency maximum was accepted at draft creation
and only rejected later at finalize. Mirror validate_custom_price_amount
and reject it up front.

subject: fix(order): notify on off-session draft order creation and finalization (#12132)
message:
fix(order): notify on off-session draft order creation and finalization (#12132)

* feat(order): fire order.created webhook on draft order creation

Draft orders (off-session charges) were persisted without firing any
order.created webhook, so merchants were never notified about them. Fire
it from create_draft_order. The webhook payload's status field conveys
the draft status (paid=false). We deliberately don't route through
_on_order_created, which would also enqueue a premature customer
confirmation email for an unpaid draft.

* feat(order): send confirmation email when a draft order is finalized

Since the draft flow skips the confirmation email at creation (the order
isn't charged yet), a finalized draft order previously resulted in no
confirmation email at all. Enqueue order.confirmation_email from
finalize_order once the order settles as paid, so the customer gets their
confirmation.

packages, which breaks typechecks that rely on it (e.g. server/emails,
where the Node `process` global stopped resolving). Mirror the existing
@types/node rule and ignore semver-major TypeScript bumps across all npm
ecosystems so adopting a new major is a deliberate change rather than an
auto-generated Dependabot PR. Minor/patch updates continue as normal.

subject: Normalize organization_id on subscriptions (#12121)
message:
Normalize organization_id on subscriptions (#12121)

* Chore: Add organization_id column to subscriptions - step 1

Add a denormalized organization_id column to the subscriptions table to
improve query performance when listing subscriptions by organization.
This is Phase A of a two-phase rollout, mirroring the same change made
to orders.

Phase A (this change):
- Migration adds the column as nullable (safe to run before new code
  deploys), with FK to organizations and a concurrently-created index
- Subscription creation paths (programmatic create + checkout) now set
  organization_id from the product's organization
- Backfill script (scripts/backfill_subscription_organization_id.py)
  populates existing rows from products.organization_id
- Existing queries are unchanged - they still resolve the organization
  via the product association proxy (to be updated in Phase B)

* Set lock_timeout in subscriptions organization_id migration

Add `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` to the upgrade and downgrade
functions, matching the migration template, so the locking DDL
(ALTER TABLE for the column and FK) can't induce a deadlock. The
CONCURRENTLY index build still runs in its own autocommit block.

* fix: move lock_timeout inside autocommit_block for concurrent index

* Update server/migrations/versions/2026-06-03-1200_add_organization_id_to_subscriptions.py

subject: Work with PriceSet throughout `checkout/service.py` (#12160)
message:
Work with PriceSet throughout `checkout/service.py` (#12160)

* Work with PriceSet throughout `checkout/service.py`

* Satisfy linter

* fix: honor `0` preset/prefill amounts for pay-what-you-want prices

Two pre-existing `or`-based fallbacks silently discarded a meaningful `0`:

- `calculate_upfront_amount` fell back to `minimum_amount` when a custom
  price had a configured `preset_amount` of `0`, despite the schema
  documenting `preset_amount=0` as "customer sees $0 as the default".
- `checkout_link_create` collapsed a validated `?amount=0` prefill to
  `None`, falling back to preset/minimum instead of honoring the zero on
  PWYW prices that allow it.

Both used truthiness (`or`) where the intent is "is it set?" (`is None`).
Switch to explicit `None` checks and add regression tests covering
`preset_amount=0` with a positive minimum, and a `?amount=0` link prefill
on a zero-minimum PWYW price.

subject: Make subscriptions.organization_id non-nullable (#12162)
message:
Make subscriptions.organization_id non-nullable (#12162)

* Subscriptions organization_id phase B: NOT NULL + direct relationship

Mirror the orders Phase B rollout for subscriptions, now that
organization_id has been backfilled:

- Migration makes subscriptions.organization_id NOT NULL using the
  NOT VALID / VALIDATE / SET NOT NULL pattern to avoid a long
  ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, with a safety-net backfill through products.
- Model: organization_id is non-nullable; the organization
  association proxy (via product) is replaced with a direct
  relationship.
- Repository: get_readable_statement and get_by_id_and_organization
  filter Subscription.organization_id directly instead of joining
  through Product; get_eager_options eager-loads Subscription.organization.
- Service: list() filters on the direct column and explicitly joins
  the product for sorting/eager-loading; get() uses default eager options.
- Dev scripts set organization_id so seeding satisfies NOT NULL.

* Ensure Subscription.organization is loaded wherever it's accessed

The organization association proxy (which resolved through product) was
replaced with a lazy="raise" relationship, so any access to
subscription.organization now requires it to be eagerly loaded.

- Fresh-creation paths (create, create_or_update_from_checkout) assign
  the organization relationship object directly so post-create hooks can
  read it.
- cancel_customer and the backoffice cancel/uncancel endpoints now load
  subscriptions with get_eager_options() before the cancellation flow,
  which accesses subscription.organization.
- The customer portal subscription list/get and the claimed-seats
  subscription list eager-load Subscription.organization, since the
  CustomerSubscription schema serializes it.
- get_eager_options() eager-loads Subscription.organization.
- The create_subscription test fixture assigns the organization
  relationship so tests can read subscription.organization.

* Assign organization relationship in create_subscription script

create_subscription.py reads subscription.organization right after
creating the subscription (to build the subscription_cycled system
event). With the lazy="raise" relationship, setting only
organization_id would raise on that access, so assign the
organization relationship object instead (product.organization is
already eagerly loaded).

* Fix Product.organization lazy=raise in checkout subscription creation

create_or_update_from_checkout assigned subscription.organization from
product.organization, but the checkout eager-load options load
Checkout.product without Product.organization, so reading it raised
'Product.organization is not available due to lazy=raise' in the
stripe.webhook.{setup_intent,charge}.succeeded tasks.

Assign from checkout.organization instead, which is eagerly loaded
(joinedload(Checkout.organization)) and is the same organization as the
product's. Fixes the e2e lifecycle/renewal test failures.

* Drop redundant Subscription.organization eager-load in read-only lists

The customer-portal subscription list and the claimed-seat subscription
list only serialize the organization via the nested
CustomerSubscriptionProduct.organization (product.organization), never
the top-level subscription.organization. So joinedload(Subscription.
organization) was a redundant second JOIN to organizations there.

Keep it in get_by_id, which also feeds the cancel/update/uncancel
mutations that read subscription.organization when building system
events.

Replace the waterfall allocation of a fixed discount with a proportional
split across the proratable line items. Each amount receives a share of the

fix(checkout): don't raise ArchivedPriceCheckout after charge is captured (#12250)

* Fix ArchivedPriceCheckout block on charge.succeeded fulfillment

When a Stripe charge.succeeded webhook fires for a checkout whose price
was archived after creation but before capture (e.g. during 3DS), the
funds are already captured but handle_success was refusing to create
the order and payment record, so the merchant never received the money.

Skip the archived-price guard when a Payment has been provided
(post-capture path). Pre-charge paths (free checkouts, setup intents)
still raise so we don't fulfill on archived prices when no funds have
been collected.

Co-Authored-By: u70c8551349ddf3cb <u70c8551349ddf3cb@users.invalid>

* Log warning instead of raising on archived price during fulfillment

Per review feedback, drop the ArchivedPriceCheckout exception entirely
from the fulfillment path. When a checkout reaches `handle_success`
with an archived price, we now log a warning with the checkout and
price IDs and proceed with fulfillment, regardless of payment state.

The previous guard blocked `charge.succeeded` webhooks (where funds
were already captured) from creating the order, leaving merchants
paid but customers without an order. The earlier patch narrowed the
exception to the `payment is None` case, but the no-payment path is
just a free order — there is no reason to block it either.

message:
Add backfill script converting free prices to fixed amount 0 (#12272)

Converts the existing free price rows to fixed prices with an amount of 0,
the final piece of dropping the free price type after new free prices are
already persisted that way.

Uses the shared run_batched_update helper: batches by id, commits per batch,
and loops until no rows remain, so it's safe to re-run or resume. Updating
amount_type alone reclassifies each row via the computed discriminator, so
free -> fixed and legacy_free -> legacy_fixed (the type column is untouched),
covering archived and soft-deleted rows too.

existence check before either had inserted, causing the second INSERT to
crash on the (source, external_id) unique constraint. Replace it with a
single ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING upsert and only enqueue the background job
when the row was actually inserted.

When updating a checkout with `product_id` + `product_price_id`, the
explicit-price branch in `_update_checkout` resolved the PriceSet against
`checkout.currency`. If the selected price's currency differed, no prices
matched and `NoPricesForCurrencies` bubbled up as an unhandled 500.

Mirror the creation path (`_get_validated_price`) by deriving currency
from the selected price and updating `checkout.currency` to match. The
discount/tax recalculation downstream already keys off the updated
currency, so no further changes are needed.

subject: benefit/grant: add unique scope index to prevent duplicate grants (#12398)
message:
benefit/grant: add unique scope index to prevent duplicate grants (#12398)

* benefit/grant: add unique scope index to prevent duplicate grants

Add a partial unique index on benefit_grants over
(customer_id, benefit_id, member_id, subscription_id, order_id) with
NULLS NOT DISTINCT and WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

The existing benefit_grants_smb_key constraint doesn't catch order-based
duplicates because their subscription_id is NULL and standard unique
indexes treat NULLs as distinct. Treating NULLs as equal closes that gap;
the partial predicate keeps soft-deleted grants from blocking re-grants.

Built concurrently to avoid locking writes on the large table.

* test: make customer grant deletion enqueue order-agnostic

The new ix_benefit_grants_scope_unique index changes the scan order of
list_granted_by_customer (which has no ORDER BY), so assert the enqueued
delete jobs with any_order=True. Their order is irrelevant.

subject: fix(backoffice): replace ILIKE with GIN tsvector search in all BO list endpoints (#12402)
message:
fix(backoffice): replace ILIKE with GIN tsvector search in all BO list endpoints (#12402)

* fix: use GIN tsvector search in backoffice endpoints (fixes #106 in polar-internal)

Replace ILIKE '%query%' scans with `search_vector @@ websearch_to_tsquery(...)` in
backoffice list endpoints (orders, customers, subscriptions, products, benefits).
The orders endpoint joined Order × Customer × Product × Organization and ILIKE'd
across four columns on every row, defeating B-tree indexes and timing out at 30s.

Mirrors the pattern already in polar/search/service.py: 'simple' config for
Customer/Order vectors, 'english' for Product/Benefit, with an ILIKE fallback on
Customer.email (not in any tsvector) and on Organization name/slug (no tsvector).

Co-Authored-By: u70c8551349ddf3cb <u70c8551349ddf3cb@users.invalid>

* fix(backoffice): drop Customer.email ILIKE fallback now that email is in search_vector

PR #12405 added `email` to Customer.search_vector, so the
`search_vector @@ websearch_to_tsquery('simple', query)` predicate now
covers what the ILIKE fallback used to. Removing the redundant ILIKE
keeps queries on the GIN index.

subject: fix(oauth2): fall back to user-scoped tokens for clients without default_sub_type (#12436)
message:
fix(oauth2): fall back to user-scoped tokens for clients without default_sub_type (#12436)

`default_sub_type` is not an RFC 7591 registered claim, so authlib strips it
from the metadata of every dynamically-registered (DCR) client. The persisted
client_metadata therefore never contains the key, and the model property's
KeyError fallback is the effective default for these clients. It was still
`organization`, so newly-registered DCR clients (e.g. MCP integrations) forced
organization selection — and, for members lacking `organization_manage` (#12361),
forced organization creation — instead of issuing a user-scoped token.

Flip the fallback to `user`, matching the intent of #12415 (which only changed
the Pydantic schema default — a value that never reaches client_metadata) and
the 2025-10-16 migration that backfilled existing clients to `user`.

feat: add offboarded merchant status (#12542)

* feat(organization): add offboarded merchant status

Introduce a terminal `offboarded` org status. An org auto-transitions
from `offboarding` to `offboarded` 120 days after its last paid order
(falling back to the offboarding-entry date). In that state new payments
are blocked, payouts are released and auto-processed, and the merchant is
emailed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(organization): address review feedback on offboarded status

- Lock the org row (FOR UPDATE) before the offboard transition so a
  concurrent admin status change isn't clobbered.
- Send the offboarded email even if the org was blocked in the interim
  (include_blocked on the lookup).
- Rename the account-router `isActive` flag to `hasAccountAccess` since it
  now also covers the terminal offboarded state.
- Tests: mock enqueue_job in the no-orders transition test; assert the
  email's account_url.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(organization): lock offboard candidates at the SELECT

Move the row lock from a per-row `session.refresh(..., with_for_update=True)`
inside the service loop to a single `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE OF organizations`
on the candidate query.

A concurrent admin status change either commits before our SELECT (the row
falls out of the WHERE clause) or waits behind the lock — eliminating the
read/transition race without the per-row recheck dance. Same pattern as
`BillingEntryRepository.lock_pending_by_subscription`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(organization): require both chargeback and wind-down gates before offboarding

Anchor the 120-day offboarding period on the *later* of the last paid
order and the offboarding-entry date (`GREATEST`), instead of the last
paid order alone (`COALESCE`).

Without this, an org freshly put into offboarding whose last payment is
already past the chargeback window would transition to `offboarded` on
the very next cron run — going from payments-on to payments-off in days
with no merchant wind-down period. With the fix, both gates must clear:
chargeback risk is past *and* the merchant has had their 120-day
wind-down in offboarding. Orgs with no paid orders still use
`status_updated_at` alone (PG `GREATEST` skips NULLs).

Adds two regression tests: the resumeset scenario (old payment, recent
offboarding → skipped) and the mirror (old offboarding, recent payment
→ skipped). Renames `test_old_paid_order_transitions` to
`test_both_anchors_old_transitions` to reflect the new semantics.

subject: Change revenue tile metrics to 29-day window instead of 1 month (#12549)
message:
Change revenue tile metrics to 29-day window instead of 1 month (#12549)

* fix(app): use rolling 30 days for home Revenue tile

The home Revenue tile derived its start date with `subMonths(new Date(), 1)`,
which steps back a full calendar month rather than 30 days. Depending on the
month this produced a 28–32 day window (e.g. May 21 → June 21 inclusive = 32
days) instead of the advertised "30 Days".

Use `subDays(new Date(), 29)` so the inclusive day range covered by the metrics
API is exactly 30 days, matching the sibling CatalogueTile's N-1 inclusive
pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ajtgi9g94fKWhNqBfeSLVy

* fix(metrics): correct off-by-one in rolling 30-day windows

The metrics API treats start_date/end_date as inclusive day bounds, so a
rolling "N days" window must start N-1 days back to cover exactly N daily
buckets (today included). Several places were a day off:

- getMetricsRangeDates('30d'): subDays(30) covered 31 days. Now subDays(29).
  This is the shared helper behind the app Metrics screen and the web
  Metrics dashboard.
- Widget fetchMetrics/fetchAllMetrics: byAdding -days covered N+1 days for the
  "Last 7/30/90 days" picker. Now -(days - 1).

Also fix the trend comparison's previous period, which shared its boundary
day with the current period (double-counting that day): it now ends the day
before the current period starts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ajtgi9g94fKWhNqBfeSLVy

* Revert widget Swift change to keep this branch OTA-shippable

The widget off-by-one fix lives in native Swift, which can't ship via an OTA
update. Revert it here so only the JS/TS metrics fixes go out; the widget fix
will need a native build.

subject: feat(worker): add DB-less broker entrypoint for DB-free queues (#12547)
message:
feat(worker): add DB-less broker entrypoint for DB-free queues (#12547)

The tinybird.ingest task only forwards events to Tinybird's HTTP API and
never queries PostgreSQL, but the worker still opened a database engine/pool
at boot because SQLAlchemyMiddleware was registered unconditionally.

Parameterize get_broker(database=...) to optionally drop SQLAlchemyMiddleware,
and add a polar.worker.run_without_db entrypoint that sets a DB-less broker as
the global broker before tasks are imported.

This is code-only: it ships the entrypoint so it's present in the deployed
image. A follow-up changes the worker start_command to use it, which must land
only after this is deployed.

organization-review website collector (with a shadow-comparison mode).

- Remove the ORGANIZATION_REVIEW_SCRAPER setting and the playwright
  dependency (relock).
- Remove the Playwright Docker stage and its CI build/push; the dedicated
  "playwright worker" Render services no longer need the chromium image,
  so fold them into the regular worker deploy list.
- Drop the local chromium install from the dev worker startup.
- Prune the Playwright/shadow collector tests.

subject: fix(subscription): cancel past_due subscriptions and void pending orders on customer deletion (#12644)
message:
fix(subscription): cancel past_due subscriptions and void pending orders on customer deletion (#12644)

When a customer is deleted, `cancel_customer` only canceled subscriptions in
`trialing`/`active` status (via `list_active_by_customer`), skipping `past_due`
ones. A `past_due` subscription with a pending order therefore kept being retried
by dunning until the final failed payment revoked it — collecting from a deleted
customer instead of voiding the order, and only canceling on that last failure.

Cancel all billable subscriptions (`trialing`, `active`, `past_due`) instead, via
a new `list_billable_by_customer` repository method. Immediate revocation already
voids pending orders through `_on_subscription_revoked`, so this also stops the
collection attempts.

message:
fix(downloadables): make uniqueness member-aware (#12556)

* fix(downloadables): make uniqueness member-aware

Move uniqueness from (customer_id, file_id, benefit_id) to a
member-aware unique index on (customer_id, file_id, benefit_id,
member_id) with NULLS NOT DISTINCT, mirroring benefit_grants. Each
member holding the benefit now gets their own downloadable row, so
members of a shared customer no longer collide on a single shared
row.

The grant service includes member_id in the upsert key, and revoke is
member-scoped. A standalone backfill script materializes per-member
rows for existing grants; the migration builds the new index
CONCURRENTLY before dropping the old constraint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(downloadables): align unique index with benefit_grants

Make the member-aware index a partial unique index
(WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) alongside NULLS NOT DISTINCT, matching the
benefit_grants scope index, and rename it to the ix_ index convention
(ix_downloadables_scope_unique). Thread an optional index_where through
upsert_many so the ON CONFLICT arbiter matches the partial index, and
scope the backfill's ON CONFLICT / NOT EXISTS to non-deleted rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(downloadables): order scope index customer, member, file, benefit

Lead the unique index with (customer_id, member_id, ...) so a member's
rows within a customer are a usable index prefix, while keeping
customer_id leading. Uniqueness and ON CONFLICT inference are
order-independent, so this is purely an access-pattern choice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address cubic review feedback (iteration 1)

Add a full index on downloadables.customer_id. The scope unique index
is partial (deleted_at IS NULL), so it no longer fully covers
customer_id for FK cascade deletes or soft-deleted lookups; restore
full coverage with a dedicated index, matching benefit_grants.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address cubic review feedback (iteration 2)

Make the downgrade atomic: restore the old unique constraint before
dropping the new indexes, all in one transaction, so a failed
downgrade rolls back to the partial unique index instead of leaving
downloadables with no uniqueness guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(migration): re-chain downloadables migration after main rebase

Repoint down_revision from 54267f23e641 to e59a12239bc2
(add_user_session_organizations, merged to main) to resolve the
multiple-heads error, and rename the file to a post-parent timestamp.

* fix: address cubic review feedback (iteration 3)

Backfill: replace the per-batch global DISTINCT/NOT EXISTS rescan with
keyset pagination over benefit_grants.id (a stable key on a table the
backfill never writes), so each batch reads a bounded slice instead of
re-scanning the whole join.

Downgrade: drop the unbounded dedupe DELETE. The rollback is now
operationally gated — recreating the customer-level constraint fails
loudly if per-member duplicates remain, rather than silently deleting
member downloadables, and runs atomically so uniqueness is never absent.

subject: Fix dunning lifecycle check to use order status instead of paid flag (#12744)
message:
Fix dunning lifecycle check to use order status instead of paid flag (#12744)

* Fix void orders incorrectly shown as dunning-failed

isOrderInDunningLifecycle used !order.paid, which is true for draft,
pending and void orders. Void orders are terminal and excluded from
dunning processing on the backend (Order.is_void.is_(False)), but the
frontend predicate would treat administrative voids with a failed
payment as "in dunning lifecycle", causing isOrderDunningFailed to show
a misleading "Payment couldn't be recovered" banner.

Check order.status === 'pending' explicitly so only dunning-eligible
orders are considered, aligning the frontend with the backend.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGL4Gr3GdydhmvU4Dp7Kap

* Include void orders in dunning lifecycle for failed recovery

When dunning exhausts its retries, the subscription is revoked and its
pending orders are voided (subscription.revoke -> _on_subscription_revoked
-> order.void_pending_orders_for_subscription). The terminal "payment
couldn't be recovered" state is therefore a void order, so restricting
isOrderInDunningLifecycle to pending orders hid the dunning-failed banner
for exactly the orders that need it.

Match both pending (actively retrying) and void (recovery gave up) while
still excluding draft and paid orders. Administrative voids don't end the
subscription, so isOrderDunningFailed's existing checks (ended_at set,
no customer cancellation reason) keep the banner off them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGL4Gr3GdydhmvU4Dp7Kap

subject: feat(worker): make health middleware db-aware (#12592)
message:
feat(worker): make health middleware db-aware (#12592)

* feat(worker): make health server database-aware

The worker health exposition server is run as a fork for every worker,
regardless of broker. Its lifespan always created a PostgreSQL engine and it
exposed two DB-querying probe routes (/webhooks, /unhandled-external-events),
so a DB-less worker (e.g. tinybird via run_without_db) still spun up a Postgres
engine/pool in its health fork — defeating the DB-free design.

Make HealthMiddleware database-aware. dramatiq registers forks by module path
and re-imports them in a fresh process (forkserver/spawn on 3.14), so the
selection is done by which module-level function is registered: get_broker
passes its database flag to HealthMiddleware, which forks _run_exposition_server
(full app + Postgres engine) or _run_exposition_server_without_db (Redis-only
liveness, no engine, no DB routes).

subject: feat: auto-cancel subscriptions for wound-down organizations (#12749)
message:
feat: auto-cancel subscriptions for wound-down organizations (#12749)

* feat: auto-cancel subscriptions for wound-down organizations

After an organization has been denied, blocked, or offboarded for longer
than a configurable delay (7 days), a daily job cancels its customers'
billable subscriptions. Customers are intentionally not emailed, since
the cancellation results from the merchant being shut down rather than a
customer- or merchant-initiated action.

The per-org job re-checks the organization status at execution time and
is idempotent at the subscription level, so a reactivated org is skipped
and duplicate/concurrent runs are safe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: trim verbose comments on the subscription auto-cancellation code

Keep only the non-obvious rationale (offboarded vs offboarding, the
no-email reason, the execution-time status re-check, idempotency) and
drop narration that restates the code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden org subscription auto-cancellation against concurrency and scale

- Lock the organization row (FOR UPDATE) when re-checking its status, so a
  concurrent admin reactivation or a duplicate per-org job cannot cancel a
  reinstated org's subscriptions or duplicate cancellation side effects.
- Cancel subscriptions in bounded keyset-paginated batches instead of
  materializing the whole set, so a large merchant doesn't allocate every
  subscription up front. Keyset (by id) also guarantees the drain terminates.
- Anchor the scan on coalesce(status_updated_at, created_at) so a terminal org
  with a legacy null status_updated_at is still wound down.
- Assert the customer.state_changed side-effect job in the cancellation test;
  add tests for batched draining and the created_at fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: stream org subscriptions for cancellation instead of keyset paging

Use repository.stream() to iterate an organization's billable subscriptions
during wind-down: batching is implicit via yield_per, there's a single loop,
and it removes the reliance on sorting random UUIDs that keyset pagination
required. The org-row FOR UPDATE lock still guards against concurrent
reactivation and duplicate jobs.

subject: fix(subscription): batch org subscription cancellation to avoid 60s timeout (#12785)
message:
fix(subscription): batch org subscription cancellation to avoid 60s timeout (#12785)

cancel_for_organization cancelled every billable subscription of an org in
one task within a single transaction committed only at the end. For a large
org the loop exceeded the worker's 60s time limit, the transaction rolled
back without committing any progress, and the retry restarted from scratch
and timed out again, looping indefinitely.

Process subscriptions in bounded batches (default 50), committing each batch
and re-enqueueing the job while subscriptions remain. Cancelled subscriptions
drop out of the billable query, so each run resumes where the last stopped;
the work is idempotent and resumable.

subject: fix(checkout): populate customer name from cardholder name when unset (#12853)
message:
fix(checkout): populate customer name from cardholder name when unset (#12853)

* fix(checkout): populate customer name from cardholder name when unset

An existing customer without a name (e.g. created through the API without
one, or matched by email) never received a name during checkout, because
customer.name was only written for newly created customers. As a result
billing_name — which falls back to name — stayed null, so orders had no
billing name and invoices could neither auto-generate nor be created via
the API.

Set customer.name from the checkout/cardholder name whenever the customer
has no name yet, regardless of whether it was just created. Existing
customers that already have a name are still protected from being
overwritten by the cardholder name (e.g. a company customer paid for by an
employee), preserving the previous team-name fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UxtYmEsYmo9vkpmm3bNr9C

* scripts: backfill customer.name and order.billing_name

Add two batched, idempotent backfill scripts to retroactively populate the
names that the recent checkout fix now sets going forward.

backfill_customer_name: sets customer.name from the earliest succeeded
checkout that carried a name (COALESCE(customer_billing_name,
customer_name), mirroring checkout confirmation). Only fills customers with
no name — never overwrites an existing one, so company/team names paid for
by an employee are left intact.

backfill_order_billing_name: sets order.billing_name from the order's
customer (COALESCE(billing_name, name)) for orders that were snapshotted
from a then-nameless customer, so those historical orders can finally
generate invoices. Run after backfill_customer_name. Orders still missing a
billing_address remain un-invoiceable — that's a separate gate.

Both use the is_distinct_from(computed) predicate for a self-terminating,
rerunnable loop that never writes NULL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UxtYmEsYmo9vkpmm3bNr9C

* scripts: address review on backfill scripts

- helper.run_batched_update: accept an optional injected session so testable
  backfills can reuse it instead of reimplementing the engine/loop/progress
  boilerplate. Backward compatible — the default (no session) path is
  unchanged, each batch still opens its own session on a dedicated engine.

- backfill_customer_name / backfill_order_billing_name: delegate to
  run_batched_update instead of duplicating the batched-update loop.

- Drop the redundant `name IS NULL` / `billing_name IS NULL` predicate: it is
  implied by `col IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(col, <source>)`, which is only true
  when col is null and a source value exists (IS DISTINCT FROM is null-safe:

IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints return empty (transient outage), the check will

Add request_timeout_ms = 30000 (30 seconds) to both data.http resources

* fix(terraform): replace check block with postcondition on data sources

Replace the module-level check block with postcondition blocks on each
data.http source. Postconditions are evaluated after the data is fetched and
will fail the plan if Cloudflare's endpoints return empty content, preventing
a silent outage where forwarded_allow_ips becomes empty and blocks all traffic.

The check block approach was insufficient as it did not properly fail the plan
in all cases. Postconditions on the data sources themselves ensure that a
bad fetch actually stops the plan.

checked for non-empty body, which would pass for non-200 responses (503,

fix(subscription): handle archived prices when applying scheduled product update (#12907)

When a scheduled product change's prices in the subscription's currency are
archived before the change is applied, PriceSet.from_product raised
NoPricesForCurrencies uncaught during cycle(), leaving the subscription
permanently locked (scheduler_locked_at never cleared).

apply_update() now resolves the new prices before mutating the subscription so
a raise leaves it untouched, and cycle() catches NoPricesForCurrencies, discards
the stale pending update, and cycles on the current product.

Replace ordinal formatting with plural-aware interval counts (#12915)

* Fix interval count on checkout using ordinal instead of cardinal

Multi-interval subscription prices rendered the interval count as an
ordinal ("$29.99 / 3rd mo", "prix / 3e mois" in French) where a billing
period is meant. Use the plain cardinal count ("/ 3 mo", "/ 3 mois") in

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HvwwELRnNWcWBMM1nPg88H

Follow-up to the ordinal fix: gluing the raw count to intervals.short
produced ungrammatical labels in locales whose short unit is a full
word ("3 mese" in Italian, "3 mês" in Portuguese) and an ambiguous

from AmountLabel and CheckoutTrialHeroPrice, so each locale controls
the plural form and spacing ("3 mesi", "3 meses", "3ヶ月", "3개월").

* feat(slack): read encrypted SlackApp secrets with plaintext fallback

Route every SlackApp secret read (client_secret, signing_secret,
bot_token) through async accessors that prefer the encrypted column and
fall back to the plaintext column, so rows not yet backfilled keep
working. Covers the credentials-validation flow, OAuth install exchange,
workspace-user listing, the events webhook signature check, and the
shared-channel benefit provisioning/archive paths. Next step of the
secrets-encryption rollout (RFC Appendix C).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(slack): route bot-token install guards through get_bot_token()

The "is it installed?" guards in the shared-channel benefit strategy and
the workspace-users endpoint still checked the plaintext `bot_token`
column while consumers read the token via `get_bot_token()` (which
prefers the encrypted column). A row whose token lives only in the
encrypted column would be wrongly reported "not installed". Route the
guards through the accessor so guard and consumption agree.

`_get_installed_integration` now returns the resolved token alongside the
integration, so provisioning decrypts once instead of twice and drops the
`cast`.

message:
Strip empty properties from custom field inputs (#12935)

* Allow clearing custom field help text, label and placeholder

Custom field form properties (form_label, form_help_text,
form_placeholder) could be set but never cleared: the frontend rejected
empty inputs with a minLength rule and the API rejected empty strings
via NonEmptyString validation.

Treat empty values as "unset" on both sides:

- Frontend: drop the minLength rules on the form input option fields
  and strip empty-string properties before submitting create/update
  requests, so cleared inputs remove the key from properties.
- Server: add a BeforeValidator on the create/update properties schemas
  that drops empty-string and null values before validation, so API
  consumers can also clear a property by sending "" or null. Stored
  values remain non-empty and the OpenAPI schema is unchanged.

message:
feat(terraform): add Cloudflare IP ranges module with Render proxy CIDR (#12941)

* feat(terraform): add Cloudflare IP ranges module for forwarded_allow_ips (#12867)

* feat(terraform): add Cloudflare IP ranges module for forwarded_allow_ips

Add a new cloudflare_ips module that fetches Cloudflare's published IPv4
and IPv6 ranges from their public endpoints and outputs them as a
comma-separated string suitable for use with forwarded_allow_ips.

Integrate the module into production, sandbox, and test environments to
restrict incoming traffic to Cloudflare's IP ranges instead of allowing
all IPs (*).

Generated by Mistral Vibe.
Co-Authored-By: ua7bfde7c38b9e917 <ua7bfde7c38b9e917@users.invalid>

* fix(terraform): add check block to validate Cloudflare IP ranges are not empty

Add a check block to the cloudflare_ips module that validates at least one
IP range was successfully fetched from Cloudflare's endpoints. If both
IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints return empty (transient outage), the check will
fail the Terraform plan rather than silently setting forwarded_allow_ips
to an empty string, which would block all traffic.

Generated by Mistral Vibe.
Co-Authored-By: ua7bfde7c38b9e917 <ua7bfde7c38b9e917@users.invalid>

* fix(terraform): add request_timeout_ms to Cloudflare IP data sources

Add request_timeout_ms = 30000 (30 seconds) to both data.http resources
fetching Cloudflare IP ranges. Without an explicit timeout, the hashicorp/http
provider has no default timeout and Terraform will hang indefinitely if
Cloudflare's endpoints are unresponsive.

Generated by Mistral Vibe.
Co-Authored-By: ua7bfde7c38b9e917 <ua7bfde7c38b9e917@users.invalid>

* fix(terraform): replace check block with postcondition on data sources

Replace the module-level check block with postcondition blocks on each
data.http source. Postconditions are evaluated after the data is fetched and
will fail the plan if Cloudflare's endpoints return empty content, preventing
a silent outage where forwarded_allow_ips becomes empty and blocks all traffic.

The check block approach was insufficient as it did not properly fail the plan
in all cases. Postconditions on the data sources themselves ensure that a
bad fetch actually stops the plan.

Generated by Mistral Vibe.
Co-Authored-By: ua7bfde7c38b9e917 <ua7bfde7c38b9e917@users.invalid>

* fix(terraform): add HTTP status code check to postconditions

Add self.status_code == 200 to both postconditions to ensure that only
successful HTTP responses are accepted. Previously, the postcondition only
checked for non-empty body, which would pass for non-200 responses (503,
404, etc.) containing HTML error content. This would get parsed as garbage
IP ranges, setting forwarded_allow_ips to invalid values and blocking all
traffic.

subject: feat(compass): live insights API over metrics (#12973)
message:
feat(compass): live insights API over metrics (#12973)

* feat(compass): live insights API over metrics

Add Compass, a live-computed narration layer on top of the metrics service
that surfaces prioritized, explained insights about an organization.

- 8 rule-based detectors (MRR, subscribers, ARPU, churn, trials, gross
  margin, cost per user, checkout conversion) over a signals layer built on
  the existing metrics service. Detectors are pure and unit-tested.
- GET /v1/compass/insights, gated per-organization by the `compass_enabled`
  feature flag; reuses the `metrics_read` scope. Fully stateless — no
  persistence.
- Seed cohorts + a `compass_diag` script for local verification.

Frontend wiring follows in a separate PR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* generate api

* remove compass diag

* test(compass): use fixed UUIDs in parametrize for xdist stability

parse_insight_key parametrize cases called uuid.uuid4() at collection
time, so each pytest-xdist worker collected different test ids and the
CI run aborted with "Different tests were collected between workers".
Use fixed UUID literals so collection is deterministic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compass): require two full windows in conversion detector

The checkout conversion detector compares a trailing 30-day window against
the prior 30 days, but the guard only required >30 periods. With 31-59
periods the prior slice silently truncated to a partial window while the
insight still claimed "the prior 30 days", yielding an unequal-length
comparison. Require two full windows (`< 2 * _WINDOW_DAYS`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(compass): move metric-series readers to the metrics module

Address PR review:
- series / latest / value_n_periods_ago / sum_last_n_periods now live as free
  functions in polar.metrics.aggregation, so any metrics consumer can reuse
  them and they're compartmentalised with Metrics rather than Compass. Kept as
  free functions (not methods on MetricsResponse) so the response schema stays
  data-only.
- MetricSignal.drivers_dimension is typed with a DriverDimension enum instead
  of a bare str.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(compass): clarify the signal-layer docstring

The "target architecture" wording read as if signals might stop being
metrics-based. Reword to make explicit that the source is always the metrics
service (Postgres + Tinybird); only how the current-vs-baseline shape is
derived could change (Python diffing today vs dedicated Tinybird pipes later).
Also fix a stale line: the per-period readers now live in
polar.metrics.aggregation, not on MetricsResponse.

* fix(compass): round suggested prices by currency decimal factor

The suggested price always rounded up to the next 100 smallest units, which
is "next whole dollar" for cent-based currencies but over-rounds
zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW) to the next 100 units. Round by the
currency's decimal factor instead: next dollar for cent currencies, next
yen for zero-decimal ones.

Publicizes kit.currency.get_currency_decimal_factor (was private with an

The insight body formatted prices with the Compass USD formatter
(hardcoded $ and /100), so a JPY product's ¥5,000 price displayed as $50

fix(seo): noindex the authenticated customer portal (#13015)

The customer portal layout set no robots metadata, so every
/[organization]/portal/* route inherited index: true from the parent
(main) layout, and robots.ts only disallowed /dashboard, /auth and
/verify-email. That left hundreds of thin, per-merchant, auth-gated
pages eligible for indexing, which dilutes the domain and can leak
merchant slugs into search results.

Add a noindex/nofollow robots metadata export on the portal layout —
the same group-level pattern already used by the checkout and embed
layouts — so the whole portal subtree is excluded from search. Using a
meta robots tag (rather than a robots.txt disallow) keeps the pages
crawlable enough for engines to actually see the noindex directive.

subject: feat(compass): scope-aware assistant core with generative UI blocks (#13017)
message:
feat(compass): scope-aware assistant core with generative UI blocks (#13017)

* feat(compass): scope-aware assistant core with generative UI blocks

The Compass assistant: an agentic chat endpoint over the merchant's own
organization, built on Pydantic AI + the Pydantic AI Gateway (the
organization_review pattern).

- SSE endpoint POST /v1/compass/assistant streaming text deltas, renderable
  block events and opaque conversation state; gated per organization by the
  compass_enabled feature flag before any model call.
- Scope safety: the agent runs under the caller's auth subject. Its toolset
  is derived from the token's granted scopes, each tool re-checks its scope
  at runtime, and the organization always comes from validated deps, never
  model arguments. Tool exceptions degrade to a polite message, never a
  traceback.
- Generative UI: tools return typed blocks from a closed discriminated
  union that the client maps to predefined components. The model places
  blocks under the claims they support via [block:N] markers parsed out of
  the token stream.
- Core tools: metrics charts, and insights with a fetch/render split so a
  broad question yields an assessment plus one or two supporting cards, not
  a card dump.

Stacked on compass-assistant-backend-1-actions. The wider tool fleet and
inference cost tracking follow in the next PR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compass): review fixes for assistant core

- Seal conversation state: the message-history blob round-trips through the
  client, so it is now HMAC-bound to the caller's organization and scope
  set. Replaying it against another organization or after a scope change is
  rejected instead of bleeding prior context into the wrong conversation.
- Metric chart windows: the inclusive date range now starts days-1 before
  today so "last N days" renders exactly N daily buckets.
- Block schemas: nullable output fields are required-but-nullable instead of
  defaulted, matching the read-schema convention and the client's types.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(compass): assistant tool fleet and self-serve inference cost tracking

Extends the assistant core with the full read-tool fleet and Polar-for-Polar
cost accounting:

- Entity tools, each gated on its own scope: orders, subscriptions,
  customers (with search), products, disputes, checkouts, refunds, payouts.
- Rankings: products by revenue (per-product metric queries so numbers match
  the dashboard), customers by paid net revenue, customers by tracked cost
  (events by-customer statistics). Customer rows carry gravatar avatars.
- get_customer_overview: one customer's card, orders and subscriptions, with
  per-section scope checks that degrade gracefully.
- Polar-for-Polar: every assistant run ingests its inference cost as a span
  on the Polar organization (root event + child with _llm/_cost metadata),
  mirroring organization reviews via a shared client helper.

Stacked on compass-assistant-backend-2-core.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compass): review fixes for the assistant tool fleet

- Customer revenue ranking subtracts refunded amounts, so partially
  refunded orders count what was actually kept.
- Customer drill-down prefers an exact email/name match and asks for
  disambiguation on several inexact matches, instead of silently picking
  the newest search hit.
- Product listing reports the real active-product count, not the page size.
- Top products by revenue selects candidates by order revenue (ids only)
  before running the per-product metric queries, so orgs with more products
  than the query budget still rank their actual top sellers; displayed
  numbers still come from the metrics layer.
- Assistant usage tracking carries a per-run idempotency key down to the
  cost-carrying child event's external_id, so task retries after a lost
  response deduplicate instead of double-counting cost.
- Compass usage enqueue tests cover zero-cost and float-cost paths like the
  organization-review sibling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compass): exclude NULL products from ranking candidates, align windows

- The candidate query grouped by nullable Order.product_id, so paid orders
  without a product could waste a candidate slot (and leak None into the id
  list). NULLs are filtered out.
- The candidate selection and the per-product metrics used off-by-one
  trailing windows (days-1 vs days), so boundary-day revenue could rank a
  product without being counted or vice versa. All assistant ranking windows
  now use the same inclusive N-day convention as the metric charts.

subject: feat(seo): generate the sitemap dynamically from the filesystem (#13020)
message:
feat(seo): generate the sitemap dynamically from the filesystem (#13020)

The sitemap was a hand-maintained array of 23 URLs that omitted every
blog post, the customer stories, and all legal pages, and stamped every
entry with lastModified: new Date() (build time) — a meaningless
freshness signal.

Derive every entry from the filesystem at build instead:
- Marketing pages by walking the (website)/(landing) subtree for
  page.tsx routes (route groups stripped, private _folders and dynamic
  [segments] skipped), plus /docs and /brand which live outside it.
- Blog posts and customer stories via getAllContent(), and legal pages
  via a new getLegalSlugs() helper, each with a real lastModified from
  the content's created_at frontmatter (omitted when absent, not faked).

New pages, posts, stories and legal docs now appear automatically. The
walk reproduces the previous marketing routes exactly; output is
de-duped and sorted for deterministic builds. Drops /careers
(301-redirects to /company) and adds no /customers index (no such page)
to avoid redirect/404 sitemap entries.

subject: fix(checkout): guard country BeforeValidator against non-string values (#13084)
message:
fix(checkout): guard country BeforeValidator against non-string values (#13084)

BeforeValidator(str.upper) on AddressInput.country (and
PayoutAccountCreate.country) called the unbound str.upper on the raw
input before Pydantic's type/nullability check ran. A client sending
customer_billing_address.country as JSON null on the checkout
create/update endpoints crashed with a raw TypeError ("descriptor
'upper' for 'str' objects doesn't apply to a 'NoneType' object"),
producing an unhandled 500 instead of a normal 422.

Replace the unsafe unbound method with a null-safe upper_if_str helper
so non-string values fall through to Pydantic's own enum validation
and surface as a proper ValidationError (422).

fix(subscription): align charge preview tax with the invoice (#13093)

* test(subscription): pin charge preview tax rules before realignment

* refactor(order): take the applicable discount as a parameter

compute_order_amounts read subscription.discount directly, which is right for
an order billing the current cycle but wrong for a caller pricing a future one,
where the discount's repetitions may already be exhausted.

Callers pass it explicitly. _create_order passes subscription.discount, so
behaviour is unchanged.

* fix(subscription): align charge preview tax with the invoice

The preview taxed only strictly positive amounts and required an explicit
tax_behavior. Two cases went untaxed as a result, in both cases understating
the amount against what the invoice records:

  - a downgrade credit of -1125 previewed a total of -1125, where the invoice
    credits the tax on it too (-1325)
  - a subscription with no tax_behavior previewed net=1000 tax=0, where the
    invoice resolves the organization default (for a FR customer, inclusive:
    net=800 tax=200)

Route the preview through compute_order_amounts so it taxes exactly as the
invoice does. It keeps its own repetition check on the discount, since it
prices the next cycle rather than the current one.

subject: payout: Add GHS minimum payout threshold for Ghana (#13121)
message:
payout: Add GHS minimum payout threshold for Ghana (#13121)

* payout: Add CRC minimum payout threshold for Costa Rica

Costa Rican Stripe accounts settle in CRC but had no entry in the payout
minimum tables, so `get_minimum_payout("crc", "CR")` fell back to the $10
default. A payout clearing the $10 gross check would still be created and
transferred, only to be rejected at Stripe's payout step with "Amount must
be no less than ₡300.00" once the amount was converted to CRC — leaving a
failed payout attempt instead of holding the balance until it's payable.

Add `crc` to ACCOUNT_PAYOUT_MINIMUM_BALANCE_PER_PAYOUT_CURRENCY at $40,
consistent with the sibling Latin-American / emerging-market currencies
(clp/bob at $40, cop at $50) added for the same cross-border reason, and
well above Stripe's ₡300 floor with FX and fee headroom. Because CR
accounts settle in CRC, the per-currency entry is the correct lever;
max(currency_min, country_min) then returns $40, so no redundant CR entry
in the per-country table is needed.

Small CRC balances now raise InsufficientBalance (surfacing the minimum to
the merchant) instead of producing a failed Stripe payout attempt.

Ref: polarsource/feedback#251

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019VyMLmkUnSCEZQL47NmM2m

* payout: Correct payout minimum currency from CRC to GHS

The reported Stripe rejection was "Amount must be no less than ₵300.00" —
the ₵ Ghana cedi sign (U+20B5), not the ₡ Costa Rican colón sign (U+20A1).
The failure is for Ghanaian payouts (GHS), not Costa Rican (CRC).

CRC never fit: ₡300 ≈ $0.60, already covered by the $10 default. GHS does:
at ~11.5 GHS/USD, Stripe's ₵300 floor is ≈ $26 — above the $10 default, so
a payout clearing the gross check gets created and transferred, then
rejected once converted to GHS.

Replace the `crc` entry with `ghs` at $50: a $50 gross balance nets ~$47.50
after payout fees, ≈ ₵546 at the current rate and still safely above ₵300
if the cedi strengthens, giving robust FX headroom for a volatile currency.
Because GH accounts settle in GHS, the per-currency entry is the correct
lever; no per-country entry is needed. Small GHS balances now raise
InsufficientBalance (surfacing the minimum) instead of a failed Stripe
payout attempt.

Ref: polarsource/feedback#251

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019VyMLmkUnSCEZQL47NmM2m

subject: fix: prevent identity verification race stranding verified users in pending (#13133)
message:
fix: prevent identity verification race stranding verified users in pending (#13133)

* fix: prevent identity verification race stranding verified users in pending

Stripe delivers the identity `processing` and `verified` webhooks back to
back. The two webhook tasks could run concurrently, and the `processing`
handler unconditionally wrote status `pending`, clobbering a `verified`
write. Verified users were then stuck in `pending`.

Lock the user row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) in all three identity handlers so
the concurrent tasks serialize, and stop the `processing` handler from
downgrading a terminal status (verified or failed) back to pending.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make verified the only absorbing identity status

Two follow-ups from review:

- The `failed` handler wrote unconditionally, so a late or redelivered
  `requires_input`/`canceled` webhook from an earlier attempt could
  un-verify a user who had since verified. Guard it: never overwrite
  `verified`.

- The `processing` handler treated `failed` as terminal and skipped it.
  But `failed` is retryable on the same reusable session, so a retry's
  `processing` webhook must move the user back to `pending`. Only `verified`
  is absorbing; allow `failed` -> `pending`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* payout: lock payout row FOR UPDATE in trigger_payout to prevent cancel race

The trigger_payout task loaded the payout row without FOR UPDATE, so a
queued trigger could race a concurrent cancel() (deny/block/backoffice).
Because the ORM object does not auto-refresh from another session's commit,
the status gate in trigger_stripe_payout could pass on a stale `pending`

producing a real Stripe payout for a canceled Polar payout.

subject: fix: block member session auth for soft-deleted customers (#13135)
message:
fix: block member session auth for soft-deleted customers (#13135)

MemberSessionRepository.get_by_token_hash() filtered out deleted member
sessions and members but did not require the joined Customer to be able to
authenticate. If a Customer is soft-deleted (e.g. by the transfer script)
while their Member and MemberSession records remain active, member-session
token auth would still succeed, granting access with deleted customer
credentials.

Add Customer.can_authenticate.is_(True) to the token lookup, mirroring the
existing CustomerSession authentication check.

message:
feat: disable Stripe account on organization deny or block (#13148)

* feat(backoffice): disable Stripe account on org deny/block

Add an opt-in control in the deny and block dialogs to reject the
organization's Stripe connected account. Human reviewers only; the AI
auto-deny path never triggers it. Picking a violated AUP section
suggests the matching Stripe reject reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(backoffice): simplify deny-dialog error and verdict checks

Flatten the combined-error build into explicit appends and drop the
redundant .value on the AI verdict comparison.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(payout_account): use read session for reject_stripe_account

The reject task only reads the payout account before calling Stripe, so
take AsyncReadSession and use AsyncReadSessionMaker, matching the
read-only task convention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style(backoffice): shorten comments and rename reject reason to Other

Trim two multi-line comments to two plain lines, and label the Stripe
"other" reject reason as "Other" instead of "Risk of delinquency".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(payout_account): harden Stripe reject task and strengthen tests

- Read the payout account from the primary session in the reject task.
  It only reads, but the rejection is permanent, so a replica-lag miss
  must not silently drop it. Reverts the earlier read-session change.
- Treat a deleted/missing Stripe account as "does not exist" in
  account_exists (catch InvalidRequestError), so the reject job skips
  instead of failing and retrying.
- Assert the deny/block decision is persisted in the opt-in Stripe tests
  (deny records a decision, block sets BLOCKED), not just the enqueue.
